verdict_rules.ALIVE: every required effect shown somewhere within ~10x of need; remaining gaps are integration/yield/measurement; revival_condition holds a kill test
verdict_rules.ALIVE-SPECULATIVE: at least one required effect contested or not shown within ~100x of need; triage_reason names it; revival_condition is the promoting measurement
verdict_rules.DEAD-PHYSICS: core claim violates a physical bound or a known show-stopper with no workaround; partial failures go in dead_subclaims instead

ideas.name: AFE-reservoir stub capacitor (Hf-free antiferroelectric ZrO2)
ideas.one_liner: Use the field-induced AFE-to-FE transition of ZrO2 (already the DRAM capacitor dielectric) as signal charge, so each stored '1' banks 10-20 uC/cm2 instead of ~3.3 uC/cm2 and the 1.3 um capacitor becomes a 200-400 nm stub.
ideas.mechanism: Tetragonal ZrO2 films 5-7 nm thick show a pinched double hysteresis loop: above ~1-1.5 MV/cm they turn polar, below a lower field they snap back. Write '1' to ~1.3 V (polar state, storing induced polarization plus linear charge); write '0' to 0 V (never crosses the forward field). Precharge the bitline low (~0.35 V, below the backward switching voltage) instead of VARY/2, so a '1' dumps its polarization onto the bitline as the film relaxes while a '0' gives only linear charge. The backward branch is a near-constant-voltage plateau: leakage drains polarization before the node voltage droops, a built-in charge reservoir. Electrode work-function asymmetry (TiN/W or TiN/Mo) or fixed charge shifts the loop to tune the plateau voltage. Same ALD ZrO2/TiN tool set as today, applied to a much shorter pillar or a short horizontal capacitor in a 3D tier.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 storage-capacitor charge wall (AR 60-75 pillars); A1 #2 3D cell (capacitor length per tier); A1 #4 capital via HAR etch and deep ALD; A2 Hf chokepoint (Hf-free).
ideas.step_change_claim: 3-6x signal charge per um2 of capacitor wall -> capacitor height 1,300 nm -> 210-420 nm (AR 62 -> 10-20) at equal signal; up to ~3x retention stretch from the plateau; horizontal 3D capacitor 3-6x shorter.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Today's wall: EOT 0.55 nm with VARY/2 = 0.525 V swing gives 3.3 uC/cm2 of signal; the 1b pillar (d 21.1 nm, h 1.3 um) holds 2.84 fC = 17,700 e- [A1]. AFE: signal = usable fraction x P_ind + half the linear swing (k 38, 6 nm, 1.3 -> 0.35 V). P_ind 15/20/25 uC/cm2 at 50/60/70% usable gives 10.2/14.7/20.2 uC/cm2 = 3.1/4.4/6.1x, so the pillar for 2.84 fC is 422/292/213 nm. Plateau: a 300 nm stub banks 1.5-2.0 fC vs a 0.84 fC linear droop budget, so retention stretches up to ~3x if the backward branch is sharp. Endurance need: 4.9e9 refresh cycles in 10 yr at 64 ms (3.2e8 at 1 s refresh), hot row ~1.6e14. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-01)

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known: AFE ZrO2/HZO non-volatile memory (NaMLab-type patent, KAIST AFTJ, Korean Hf0.3Zr0.7O2 work) and MPB high-k HZO exist. Using the AFE transition as DRAM signal charge, with low-precharge sensing and the backward branch as a retention reservoir, was not found in public literature [UNVERIFIED].
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Endurance: AFE films are reported at ~1e9-1e10 cycles, while every write or read of a '1' cycles the transition and a DRAM cell needs ~1e12-1e15. (2) The switching-field spread across grains in a 6 nm film smears the plateau and the read threshold, and wake-up or fatigue shifts it. (3) Back-switching speed under 10 ns and leakage at the 1.3 V write level are unproven at DRAM pillar scale.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Only '1' states cycle; with an IGZO access device (refresh >=1 s) refresh adds only 3e8 cycles in 10 yr. Add write-back caching for hot rows, and use Zr-rich or La/N-doped ZrO2, which the patent says outlasts HfO2. (2) Columnar, grain-engineered ALD; write-verify; self-referenced reads that compare a cell to itself after a reference write. (3) If back-switching is slow, run just below the forward field as a nonlinear k booster (a weaker 1.5-2x version).
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Months 0-9: planar and trench TiN/ZrO2/TiN MIM capacitors (5-8 nm, asymmetric electrodes) in a university ALD line. Measure PUND switching charge at 5-100 ns, the plateau under constant-current discharge, and endurance to 1e12 at 85 C. Months 9-20: 300 nm pillar arrays plus BEOL IGZO access TFTs in 1T1C test arrays read by a low-precharge sense circuit on a pad-level test board. Budget ~$380k: ALD/etch fab time $90k, WGFMU-class pulse tester and probe station $150k, TCAD/Landau modelling $20k, one postdoc-year $120k.
ideas.resource_angle: Hafnium-free (A2 flags HZO capacitors at 14-41% of world Hf); Zr is already used and abundant. A 3-6x shorter capacitor cuts HAR etch time, fluorocarbon (PFAS-adjacent) etch gas and deep-hole ALD cycles. No EUV change.
ideas.us_buildable: NCSU Nanofabrication Facility, Purdue Birck, Penn Singh Center (ALD + PUND), NY CREATES Albany 300 mm ALD/etch for pillars, Sandia MESA (ferroelectric capacitor experience).
ideas.triage_reason: Field-induced AFE->FE polarization in 5-7 nm ZrO2 (P_ind 15-25 uC/cm2 vs the 3.3 uC/cm2 linear signal) is established, and using the backward-branch plateau as a charge reservoir is sound electrostatics. Unproven: endurance of the full transition at ns pulses. Best seen this session: ~5e9 field cycles for T-phase ZrO2 (JMCC 2024 supplement) and ~1e8 for a confined 12 nm AFE film (NTU 2026), against 3.2e8 (1 s refresh) to 6.9e13 (hot row, 1% duty) cycles needed (C0-1): a 10-1e4x gap. Grain-to-grain switching-field spread in 6 nm films also smears the plateau.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a 5-7 nm ZrO2 MIM stub shows >=1e12 full AFE cycles at 10 ns pulses and 85 C with <10% loss of released charge, and back-switching <=10 ns. Kill test: <1e10 cycles with no upward composition trend (Zr-rich, La/N-doped).
ideas.claim_short: 3-6x signal charge/area; capacitor 1.3 um -> 0.21-0.42 um; Hf-free

ideas.name: Temperature-hardened negative-capacitance stub (FE/DE superlattice)
ideas.one_liner: Put a ferroelectric HZO layer in series with the ZrO2/Al2O3 dielectric, designed so its negative capacitance stays stabilized from -10 to 125 C; the stack holds 2.5-4.7x more charge per area than the dielectric alone.
ideas.mechanism: A ferroelectric biased in the unstable middle of its Landau double well has negative differential capacitance C_FE < 0. In series with a dielectric (C_DE) and with |C_FE| > C_DE, the total capacitance C_DE/(1 - r) exceeds C_DE, where r = C_DE/|C_FE|. The stack is an ALD superlattice of Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (or Zr-rich HZO) with ZrO2/Al2O3 layers on TiN, deposited in the same pillar or short horizontal capacitor. The twist is designing r against temperature: |C_FE| follows Curie-Weiss behaviour, so r is set to ~0.85 at the cold corner and falls to ~0.6 at 125 C. The capacitor then never crosses into hysteresis and still gives >=2.5x at the hot corner.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor charge wall; A1 #2 3D (capacitor length per tier).
ideas.step_change_claim: 2.5x (125 C) to 4.7x (25 C) capacitance per area -> pillar 1,300 -> ~430-650 nm for equal Cs; or the same height with a ~2.5-4x bigger signal at 1c/1d cell sizes.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: C_tot/C_DE = 1/(1-r): r = 0.5 -> 2.0x, 0.6 -> 2.5x, 0.7 -> 3.3x, 0.8 -> 5.0x. With Curie-Weiss T0 = 450 C [ESTIMATE] and r = 0.85 at -10 C: r = 0.79/0.67/0.60 at 25/85/125 C -> 4.7/3.1/2.5x. A 2x gain halves the pillar to 650 nm; 3x gives 433 nm. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-02)

ideas.novelty: KNOWN physics and target (stabilized NC: Hoffmann/NaMLab lineage; Ahn group MRS 2023 for DRAM capacitors; epitaxial HZO/Al2O3 2024). TWIST: a temperature-compensated r design and pairing with stub/horizontal 3D capacitors rather than full-height pillars.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Multi-domain formation in polycrystalline HZO turns single-domain NC into hysteresis and loss; whether static NC survives at ns read speeds is still debated. (2) Leakage and dispersion: the FE layer adds leakage paths and frequency-dependent capacitance. (3) Hf demand and wake-up/imprint drift move r over life.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Use ultrathin (2-4 nm) FE layers in a superlattice, where depolarizing fields from the adjacent dielectric suppress domains; measure at 1-100 MHz and with 10 ns charge pulses before claiming gain. (2) Keep Al2O3 blocking layers at the electrodes; the target is leakage at today's 1e-7 A/cm2 class. (3) Zr-rich FE (Hf-lean) and periodic 'reset' anneal pulses; r margins sized for end-of-life drift.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Twelve ALD superlattice splits on TiN MIM test chips (r from 0.4 to 0.9). Measure C-V from -40 to 150 C, 10 ns pulsed charge versus Al2O3/ZrO2 references, leakage, and 1e12 cycling. Then 500 nm pillars at a 300 mm partner. Budget ~$300k with university ALD access plus a cryo/hot probe station.
ideas.resource_angle: Halves HAR etch depth (capital, PFAS etch gas), but uses Hf (A2: concentrated supply). A Zr-rich FE variant reduces Hf exposure.
ideas.us_buildable: Penn Singh Center, Georgia Tech IEN, Purdue Birck, NY CREATES Albany (300 mm pillars).
ideas.triage_reason: Series-stabilized negative capacitance is allowed by Landau theory and enhancement is reported in HZO/ZrO2/Al2O3 superlattices, but whether it survives as a hysteresis-free, ns-speed small-signal effect in polycrystalline multi-domain films is contested. The 4.7x end needs |C_FE| within ~20% of C_DE, where the enhancement diverges and becomes hypersensitive to temperature and wake-up drift across 1e10 cells.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a 10 ns charge-pulse measurement (not kHz C-V) shows >=2x charge per area over a DE-only reference at 85-125 C with no hysteresis and leakage <=1e-7 A/cm2.
ideas.claim_short: 2.5-4.7x capacitance/area via stabilized NC; pillar 1.3 -> 0.43-0.65 um

ideas.name: IGZO gated-diode strip: a capacitor-module-free 3D DRAM tier ('two-gate NAND-like DRAM')
ideas.one_liner: Store the bit as electrons accumulated in an IGZO channel strip under a second 'plate' gate, a gated diode or CCD well, and read by pushing the whole packet onto the bitline; a 3D tier then needs no TiN/high-k/TiN capacitor fill, only a second word plane.
ideas.mechanism: Each tier holds a horizontal GAA IGZO (or IGO) strip with two gates: an access wordline and a plate gate. Write '1': with the wordline on and the bitline at 0 V, electrons accumulate under the positively biased plate. Write '0': with the bitline high, the well stays empty. Read: precharge the bitline, open the wordline, pull the plate low, and the stored electrons transfer completely to the bitline. A '0' moves almost nothing because a fully depleted 10 nm IGZO film has near-zero depletion capacitance. The plate is a row-shared line driven at 2.5 V, so the signal is set by the plate swing, not VARY, and the bitline can run at ~0.45 V. Built like Kioxia's SiN-replacement horizontal IGZO tiers: both gates are word-plane metal, and no lateral recess-and-fill capacitor module is needed.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 no manufacturable 3D DRAM cell (capacitor in a tier = blocker 1); A1 #1 capacitor wall; A1 #10 array voltage floor; A1 #3 leakage (IGZO).
ideas.step_change_claim: Removes the 3D capacitor module entirely. Per-tier footprint 0.011-0.016 um2 vs A1 base 0.030 um2 -> 3D density break-even falls from ~26 tiers to ~9-14 tiers. Array energy per access ~5 fJ vs ~38 fJ bitline CV2 today.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: A GAA strip 40 x 10 nm (100 nm perimeter) under a 150-200 nm plate at EOT 1.1 nm gives C_gd = 0.47-0.63 fF. The full well at a 2.0 V effective plate swing is 0.94-1.26 fC (5,900-7,800 e-), giving a 60-80 mV signal on a 64-cell local bitline (7.8 fF) with complete transfer. Signal gain vs a linear capacitor at equal C is 1.9x (IBM gated diode reported ~3-4), but EOT 1.1 vs 0.55 nm cancels it: per unit wall area it equals today's capacitor. The win is process and footprint, not charge density. Tier footprints: 50x600 nm -> 0.0173 Gb/mm2/tier (25.9 tiers to match 1b); 70x230 nm -> 13.9 tiers; 60x180 nm -> 9.3 tiers. Energy: 64-cell bitline at 0.45 V = 1.6 fJ, plate 3.8 fJ. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-03)

ideas.novelty: NEW combination: IBM's gated-diode gain cell (Luk & Dennard 2004) + CCD-style complete charge transfer + IGZO accumulation-mode strips in NAND-style horizontal tiers. No public 3D-DRAM proposal that replaces the horizontal capacitor with a plate gate on the channel was found [UNVERIFIED].
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Fresh signal is only 60-80 mV on a 64-cell local bitline, so droop budget is thin; it needs local sensing every 64 cells (bonded periphery) or B1-04 charge-transfer amplification. (2) Trap capture/emission in IGZO under the plate makes transfer incomplete and history-dependent. (3) The row-wide plate swing couples into neighbours (disturb) and costs energy if pages stay large.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Lengthen the plate (200-300 nm), raise the plate swing to 3 V, or pair with charge-transfer pre-sense (B1-04) to get >=150 mV. (2) Run a 'fat zero' background charge (classic CCD trick) and passivated IGO/HfO2 interfaces (SJTU-style 100x leakage gains). (3) Segment plate lines per sub-array and pair with sub-page activation.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Planar first: two-gate IGZO TFT strips (WL + plate, 50-200 nm plates) on 150/200 mm at a university fab. Measure transfer completeness, signal vs plate swing, retention at 85/125 C, and disturb. Then a 2-4 tier horizontal stack using SiN-replacement IGZO, read by a discrete or MPW sense chip. Budget ~$450k: fab time $150k, MPW sense chip $80k, test $120k, people.
ideas.resource_angle: Deletes the TiN/high-k/TiN lateral fill and its HAR recess etch (capital, process time, Hf/Zr). IGZO In/Ga quantities are trivial, but Ga is ~98% Chinese (A2), so prefer In-Sn-Zn or IGO/ITO-class channels. All-deposition tiers, no EUV.
ideas.us_buildable: Purdue Birck (ALD oxide channels), Georgia Tech IEN, Penn Singh Center; 300 mm stack trials at NY CREATES Albany; MPW sense die on GlobalFoundries 22FDX/12LP via MOSIS-class brokers.
ideas.triage_reason: A gated-diode/accumulation MOS capacitor on an IGZO strip, read by one charge transfer through an oxide TFT, is standard device physics (IBM gated diode; display storage capacitors). Only one transfer per read is needed, so ~99% transfer efficiency suffices (unlike B1-08). The 60-80 mV fresh signal on 64-cell local bitlines is thin but within offset-cancelled sensing; a-IGZO band-tail trapping is an engineering parameter.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: single-transfer efficiency <95% or lag >5% at 85 C on an IGZO plate-gate strip, or plate-line disturb >10% of signal per 1e5 neighbour activations.
ideas.claim_short: No 3D capacitor module; 3D break-even 26 -> 9-14 tiers; ~5 fJ/access

ideas.name: Charge-transfer pre-sense on a long bitline: sub-fF cells without shortening the bitline
ideas.one_liner: Hold the bitline at a fixed voltage with a self-biased transfer transistor and move the cell's charge onto a ~1.5 fF sense node; a 0.5 fF cell then gives ~155 mV even on a 512-cell bitline, so the capacitor can be 10x smaller with array efficiency intact.
ideas.mechanism: Conventional sensing divides the cell charge by Cs + Cbl (35 fF), so only ~7 mV survives from a 0.5 fF cell. In charge-transfer pre-sensing (Arimoto/Mitsubishi lineage) the bitline is precharged through its own transfer gate, which therefore self-biases at its own threshold and cancels Vt mismatch. When the cell dumps charge, the bitline moves a few mV, the transfer gate conducts in subthreshold, and the charge flows onto a small sense node. Gain = Cbl/C_sn. The twist is pairing this with an IGZO access device (1 aA), so a 0.3-0.5 fF cell still retains 45-75 s, and using offset-cancelled latches. The capacitor becomes a ~120 nm stub (AR ~6) or even the gate-plus-junction capacitance of a vertical channel.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor wall; A1 #4 HAR etch capital; A1 #2 3D (stub fits a tier); A1 #7 keeps array efficiency (no 4-8x more sense amps).
ideas.step_change_claim: 10x smaller storage capacitor (5.4 -> 0.5 fF; pillar 1,300 -> ~120 nm) at today's 512-cell bitline. Signal on the sense node 155 mV vs 7.5 mV conventional.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Transfer-gate gm at 100 nA bias = I/(n kT/q) = 2.5 uS, so tau = Cbl/gm = 13.9 ns; transfer efficiency is 0.76/0.88/0.96 after 20/30/45 ns. With C_sn = 1.5 fF and 30 ns: Cs 2.0/1.0/0.5/0.3 fF gives 619/309/155/93 mV, vs 28.6/14.7/7.5/4.5 mV conventional. Pillar heights 481/240/120/72 nm; signal electrons 6,550/3,280/1,640/980. Retention with IGZO 1 aA and 150 mV droop: 75 s (0.5 fF), 45 s (0.3 fF). kT/C on the sense node is 1.8 mV rms. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-04)

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known: charge-transfer pre-sensing dates to 1990s DRAM (Arimoto et al., JSSC 1997, cited in the patent family) and was dropped when capacitors were large. The new part is the combination with oxide-channel retention so the capacitor can collapse 10x, while keeping long bitlines (unlike A1 white space 1).
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Speed: subthreshold transfer adds ~20-45 ns to row access (tRCD) unless bias current rises, and higher bias worsens mismatch error. (2) Residual offset: transfer-gate mismatch and bias-current mismatch (a 100 nA bias over 30 ns moves 3 fC, 12x the signal) must cancel to <5%. (3) Soft errors and noise margin at ~1,000-1,600 signal electrons.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Two-stage transfer, boosted gate drive (the 0.5 V CT-SA paper shows +41% speed), or 256-cell bitlines (tau halves). (2) Self-biased precharge (each gate settles at its own Vt) plus a differential reference column; autozero latches. (3) BEOL IGZO cells have no Si collection volume, which cuts charge collection; add ECC; keep Cs >=0.5 fF (~1,600 e-).
ideas.million_dollar_demo: One MPW test chip (22 nm FD-SOI or 28 nm bulk, ~4 mm2) containing sense-amp banks driving programmable MIM 'cells' of 0.2-5 fF and switchable 128/256/512-cell-equivalent bitline loads. Measure signal, offset distributions over 10k columns, speed vs bias, and temperature. Then hook up BEOL IGZO 1T1C coupons from B1-01/B1-05 partners. Budget ~$250k: MPW $80-120k, board and test $60k, design tools via university.
ideas.resource_angle: Removes the HAR capacitor etch and most deep ALD (capital, fluorocarbon gas, Hf/Zr volume). Bits per wafer-hour rise, which is A2's binding constraint. Pure circuit plus oxide channel; no new scarce elements.
ideas.us_buildable: Design anywhere; MPW on GlobalFoundries (Malta, NY) or SkyWater (MN) for a 130/90 nm proof; IGZO coupons from Purdue, Georgia Tech or Penn.
ideas.triage_reason: Charge-transfer pre-sensing is demonstrated 1990s DRAM circuit physics. Bitline kTC noise on 35 fF is ~82 e- rms against 1,560 signal electrons at 0.5 fF x 0.5 V (19 sigma; 9.5 sigma even at 0.25 fF) (C0-11), so noise is not the limit. Transfer-gate and bias-current mismatch and the ~20-45 ns transfer time are circuit engineering. IGZO leakage <1 aA gives ~75 s retention at 0.5 fF.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: an MPW sense chip cannot hold residual offset <5% of a 0.25 fC packet with a tRCD penalty <=15 ns.
ideas.claim_short: Cs 5.4 -> 0.5 fF (pillar 1.3 -> ~0.12 um) on an unchanged 512-cell bitline

ideas.name: 2-bit/cell 1T1C on an oxide access device
ideas.one_liner: With an IGZO access transistor leaking <1 aA, a 1T1C cell can hold four voltage levels for ~80 s, doubling bits per cell on the existing capacitor if sensing resolves the ~55-70 mV level steps.
ideas.mechanism: Write one of four levels (0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 x VARY) through a vertical IGZO access transistor (OCTRAM/Samsung VCT style). Read by successive approximation: charge-share onto a short bitline, decide the MSB against a mid reference, then the LSB against a reference chosen by the MSB (or a time-domain ramp), then restore all four levels. A silicon cell cannot do this, because its 13 fA tail leaks a full level in milliseconds. At 1 aA the droop is 0.18 mV/s, so a 15 mV level budget lasts ~80 s. Combine with 128-cell bitlines (bonded periphery) or charge-transfer pre-sense (B1-04) for margin.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 litho-bound density (density from levels, not wavelength); A1 #1 (more bits per capacitor); A1 #3 (needs low leakage, uses it).
ideas.step_change_claim: 2x bits per cell -> 1.8-2.8x die density at the same F, depending on array efficiency (0.89-1.23 Gb/mm2 vs 0.447), with no new lithography.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Level-edge signal = (VARY/6) x Cs/(Cs+Cbl). With Cs 5.4 fF it is 24 mV at 512 cells (too small), 55 mV at 128 cells and 71 mV at 64 cells. IGZO 1 aA leakage on 5.4 fF droops 0.18 mV/s -> 15 mV lasts 81 s. Density: 2 b/cell at the 1b cell with array efficiency 0.45/0.51/0.70 gives 0.79/0.89/1.23 Gb/mm2 = 1.77/2.0/2.76x. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-05)

ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Signal per level is a third of 1-bit, so it needs short bitlines (more sense amps) or charge-transfer gain. (2) Successive-approximation read plus restore adds latency (~1.5-2x tRCD/tRAS) and energy. (3) IGZO Vt drift (PBTI/H) and capacitor variation eat the 55 mV steps; row hammer on intermediate levels is unknown.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Periphery-under-array bonding pays for sense amps (A1 #7); or 3-level cells (1.58 b) with 2x margin. (2) Hide latency with sub-page reads; use MLC for capacity tiers (CXL/HBM-capacity) where 20-30 ns more latency is acceptable. (3) Write-verify, per-row reference cells, ECC across levels.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: BEOL IGZO-TFT + MIM 1T1C mini-arrays (1-4 kb) at a university fab, read by an MPW SAR/time-domain sense chip. Map level distributions vs time at 85 C, cycling and disturb. Budget ~$400k.
ideas.resource_angle: 2x bits per wafer pass is a direct cut in capital and cleanroom hours per bit (A2 binding constraint) without EUV. Ga exposure from IGZO (prefer IGO/ITZO).

ideas.triage_reason: Four-level 1T1C was built in 1997 and failed on Si leakage, which IGZO (<1 aA) removes. 55-70 mV level steps sit far above kTC (0.38 mV) and need offset-cancelled or charge-transfer sensing; Vt drift and capacitor variation are engineering.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: level overlap gives >1e-4 raw BER after 1 s at 85 C on a 64-256-cell bitline with write-verify.

ideas.name: Vertical oxide semi-floating-gate 1T1D gain cell (4F2, capacitor-less, stackable)
ideas.one_liner: Shrink the 2T0C gain cell to one vertical oxide transistor whose floating gate is charged through a built-in high-barrier diode (the Fudan semi-floating-gate idea, rebuilt in BEOL oxides), giving a 4F2 stackable gain cell.
ideas.mechanism: A vertical ALD In2O3/IGZO channel pillar is wrapped by a metal floating gate (FG), which is wrapped in turn by a control-gate wordline. A Schottky or MIS diode (Pt/IGZO, p-NiO/IGZO heterojunction, or a thin Al2O3 tunnel diode) links the FG to the drain/bitline at the pillar top. Write: the wordline couples the FG below the bitline, the diode forward-biases and the FG charges to the bitline level. Hold: raise the wordline so the diode is reverse-biased. Read: the FG charge sets the channel current, non-destructively. The reverse current of the diode sets retention, and the cell fits in the footprint of one vertical transistor. Fudan's Si SFG (Science 2013) showed ns writes at <2 V, but its embedded TFET/diode made it large; oxide BEOL lets the diode sit vertically on top.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 (no capacitor); A1 #2 3D (1T per tier footprint); A1 #3 (oxide leakage); A1 #8 non-destructive read.
ideas.step_change_claim: 2.5x per-tier density vs 10F2 2T0C: at F = 20 nm, b x N for 1b parity falls from 3.7 to 1.5; at F = 40 nm (single-exposure ArF, no EUV) from 14.9 to 6.0 (e.g., 2 bits x 3 tiers).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Retention = C_FG x dV / I_rev with C_FG 0.3 fF, dV 0.2 V, 20x20 nm diode, A* = 41 A/cm2K2. Barrier 0.8/0.9/1.0/1.1 eV at 85 C gives 0.5 s / 13 s / 340 s / 8,700 s; at 125 C 0.03 s / 0.6 s / 11 s / 200 s. So the diode needs >=1.0-1.1 eV effective barrier (or a tunnel-oxide MIS diode). Density: 4F2 at F = 20 nm = 0.30 Gb/mm2/tier; 10F2 = 0.12. At F = 40 nm: 0.075 vs 0.030. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-06)

(3) Read-current variability of a single vertical oxide device for multi-level storage.

(2) MIS diode (1-2 nm Al2O3 tunnel layer) or p-NiO/IGZO heterojunctions; measure the Arrhenius barrier directly. (3) Write-verify plus 1-2 b/cell first.

The new requirement is a write diode with phi_B >= ~0.95 eV on an n-type oxide: thermionic reverse leakage at 85 C through a 20x20 nm diode is 1.2e-16 A at 0.8 eV (0.35 s retention for 0.2 fF/0.2 V) but 1.8e-19 A at 1.0 eV (~230 s) (C0-4). Barriers near 1 eV are within reach of oxidized-noble-metal or p-NiO/IGZO junctions but are unverified on this stack.

ideas.name: 1T + 2 tunnel-diode latch: a refresh-free static cell at near-DRAM density
ideas.one_liner: Two stacked negative-differential-resistance diodes on the storage node latch it to '0' or '1' indefinitely (the TI 1998 tunneling-SRAM idea). This removes refresh entirely, if the diodes' valley current can be brought to ~1-6 pA per cell.
ideas.mechanism: The storage node of a 1T cell sits between two series NDR diodes (resonant tunnelling or interband Esaki) tied to the supply and ground rails. Their I-V curves cross at two stable points near the rails, so the node self-restores against leakage, with no refresh, no tRFC and a non-destructive read. Van der Wagt's III-V RTD/HFET gain cell proved the latch at ~50 nW/cell. The new part is BEOL-stackable, ultra-low-current-density NDR diodes stacked on the capacitor/storage contact in ~8F2. Candidates: oxide double-barrier (Al2O3/ZnO/Al2O3 quantum well) or MIIM diodes, Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes, or vdW graphene/hBN resonant tunnelling.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh (energy 46 fJ/bit-refresh, 16-33% of idle power; 7.6-20% availability lost to tRFC); A1 #8 destructive read.
ideas.step_change_claim: Refresh energy and refresh time -> 0 (7.6% availability at 16 Gb, ~20% at 64 Gb recovered). Static standby set by valley current: break-even with today's refresh power at J_valley ~0.23 A/cm2 (25 nm diodes).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: 16 Gb die refresh power = 1.7e10 cells x 46 fJ / 64 ms = 12.2 mW. Matching it at 0.5 V needs I_valley <= 1.4 pA/cell = 0.23 A/cm2 for a 25 nm diode (J_peak 1.1 A/cm2 at PVCR 5). A 4x budget allows 5.7 pA, 0.92 A/cm2. Today: TI's ~50 nW/cell = 850 W per die (7e4x too high); InP RTD 'nA' operation ~0.5 nW = 8 W per die (700x too high). (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-07)

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known (TI/Raytheon tunneling SRAM 1998-99; molecular-RTD local-refresh proposal). [SPECULATIVE] at the required current density: no NDR diode with PVCR >=3-5 at J_peak ~1-5 A/cm2 is known to this agent.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) PVCR collapses at ultra-low current density because defect-assisted and phonon-assisted valley currents do not scale down with the resonant peak. (2) Peak-voltage uniformity across 1e10 diodes: bistability needs matched I-V curves (~10-20%). (3) Two extra stacked devices per cell, plus their temperature sensitivity (PVCR falls at 85-125 C).
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Wide-gap oxide or hBN barriers suppress thermionic valley current; the measurable target is a J_peak/J_valley map vs barrier thickness at 85 C. (2) Write-verify trims cannot fix diodes, but redundancy plus ECC can tolerate ~1e-4 bad latches, which fall back to ordinary refreshed DRAM cells (hybrid refresh map). (3) Use one NDR diode plus a linear load (a weaker latch); or an 'only-the-weak-rows' variant where latches sit only on cells that fail retention tests.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Phase 1 (12 months, ~$300k): ALD oxide double-barrier and MIIM diode splits plus Si/SiGe RITD samples. Measure I-V at 25-125 C down to pA, and PVCR vs J_peak, against the 0.2-1 A/cm2 target. Phase 2 (~$200k): latch demonstration on a MIM storage node with an IGZO access TFT, showing static hold at 85 C.
ideas.resource_angle: Deletes refresh energy (A2: use-phase energy ~16x fab energy per GB). Oxide or Si/SiGe diodes avoid III-V and Ga if the oxide route works.
ideas.us_buildable: Oregon State (ALD MIIM diodes), Ohio State (Si/SiGe RITDs), Penn State nanofab, Cornell CNF.
ideas.triage_reason: Bistable RTD latches work (TI/Raytheon TSRAM). The cell beats refresh power only if valley current is <=~1-6 pA per 25 nm diode (J_valley <=0.23 A/cm2) with PVCR >=3 at 85 C, i.e. J_peak ~1 A/cm2. No law forbids it (thermionic valley current falls below 0.2 A/cm2 for barriers >=0.5 eV, and inelastic valley tunnelling scales with the same barrier transmission), but no NDR diode at J_peak ~1 A/cm2 with PVCR >=3 has been reported.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a diode with J_peak <=5 A/cm2, PVCR >=3 at 85 C and <=20% peak-voltage spread across a wafer is shown.
ideas.claim_short: Refresh -> 0 via a static two-tunnel-diode latch at near-DRAM density

ideas.name: Vertical oxide CCD string: transistor-less 3D charge-shift memory
ideas.one_liner: Build a 3D-NAND-like stack of word planes around a vertical IGZO channel, but clock the planes as a CCD so charge packets shift up the hole to one sense amp. There is no transistor or capacitor per bit, and IGZO's near-zero thermal generation lets packets sit for seconds.
ideas.mechanism: Etch one high-aspect-ratio hole through 128-256 alternating W/Mo and SiO2 word planes (the same module as 3D NAND), and line it with a thin gate oxide and an ALD IGZO/IGO channel. Clock planes in 4 phases (2 gates per bit): each bit is a packet of ~1,000-5,000 electrons in an accumulation well. Si CCDs lose stored charge to thermal generation (dark current); wide-gap IGZO generates essentially no carriers, so packets hold, limited only by inter-well barriers and gate leakage. Reading shifts packets out of the top of the string into a charge-transfer sense amp (B1-04) on bonded periphery, and data recirculates to the bottom: a delay-line memory with 32-64-bit strings and thousands of parallel holes per line access. Planes are segmented into small blocks to keep plane RC at ~1 ns per phase.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 3D cell (no capacitor and no transistor per bit); A1 #4 litho capital (one HAR etch, no EUV); A2 white space 1 (bits added by deposition).
ideas.step_change_claim: 4.2-8.3x 1b density (1.85-3.7 Gb/mm2 at 128-256 planes) with zero per-bit devices; streaming read energy 17-67 fJ/bit; but access is serial (32-128 ns worst-case to a given bit).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Hex hole pitch 150 nm -> 0.0195 um2 per hole. 128 planes / 2 gates per bit = 64 bits per hole -> 1.85 Gb/mm2 at 0.60 efficiency (4.2x 1b); 256 planes -> 3.71 Gb/mm2 (8.3x); 3 gates/bit -> 5.5x. Gate-hole capacitance 33 aF -> 0.13 fJ per toggle at 2 V. A 64-gate string (32 bits) costs 16.7 fJ per shift step = 16.7 fJ/bit to stream out; worst latency 32 ns at 1 ns per step (128 gates: 33 fJ/bit, 64 ns). CTE must be >=0.9999: after 128 transfers 98.7% of a packet remains (0.999 leaves 88%). Interface traps under one gate: 6-57 per eV at Dit 1e11-1e12. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-08)

ideas.novelty: NEW combination [SPECULATIVE]: 1970s CCD main memories (Intel/Fairchild 16-64 kb CCD parts) [UNVERIFIED: training knowledge] + 3D NAND vertical-channel stacks + wide-gap oxide channels with negligible thermal generation. No vertical-oxide CCD memory proposal was found [UNVERIFIED].
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Charge-transfer efficiency: IGZO band-tail and interface traps capture and release electrons each transfer; CTE <0.9999 destroys packets within a few strings. (2) Serial access: DRAM-class random latency needs short strings and fast (~1 ns) plane clocks, against the large RC of NAND-style word planes. (3) Disturb and blooming between packets; recirculation means every read rewrites the string.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Fat-zero background charge, buried-channel bilayers (IGO core + IGZO cladding) to keep packets off the interface, H-passivated interfaces; measure CTE vs clock and temperature first. (2) 32-bit strings with thousands of parallel holes per 64 B line make access a fixed ~32-40 ns burst; segment planes into small blocks with Mo/Ru-free low-R metal. (3) 4-phase clocking with barrier phases; a streaming tier (LLM weights, KV cache) where sequential bursts are natural.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Months 0-8: planar overlapping-gate IGZO CCD (8-16 gates) on glass or Si at a university fab, measuring CTE vs clock rate (1-100 MHz) and temperature, and hold time at 85 C. Months 8-22: 8-16-plane vertical test stacks (W/SiO2, punched hole, ALD IGZO) at a 200/300 mm partner, read by a discrete charge amplifier. Budget ~$500k.
ideas.resource_angle: Bits by deposition, one HAR etch per stack: lowest litho intensity of any card (no EUV, ~1 critical mask per stack). Avoid Ru/Mo-scarce plane metals at volume; W is China-concentrated (A2), so watch that.
ideas.us_buildable: Purdue Birck, Penn Singh Center (planar CCD), NY CREATES Albany or SUNY Poly 300 mm for vertical stacks; Micron Boise R&D as a later partner.
ideas.triage_reason: CCD physics and 3D-NAND word-plane stacks are both proven, and IGZO's >3 eV gap makes thermal dark charge negligible. The unproven quantity is charge-transfer efficiency in an amorphous oxide channel: a 32-transfer string needs CTE >=0.9999 (0.9999^32 = 0.997), while a-IGZO band-tail and interface traps (6-57 states per gate per eV vs 1,000-8,000 e- packets, B1 estimate) could cap CTE near 0.99-0.999 without fat-zero or buried-channel tricks. This session's search found no published CTE data for any oxide-semiconductor CCD: open territory.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a planar or vertical IGZO/IGO CCD test string shows CTE >=0.9999 per transfer at >=100 MHz clocks and 85 C with fat zero.

ideas.name: Nanogap (vacuum/air) tunnel-barrier floating node: flash-like retention without oxide wear
ideas.one_liner: Isolate a gain cell's floating node with a 2.5-4 nm sealed vacuum/air gap instead of tunnel oxide; Fowler-Nordheim emission across the gap writes in ns at 6-8 V, while the trap-free gap holds charge for hours to years.
ideas.mechanism: The floating metal node (TiN or W, anchored on dielectric on one side) faces a write electrode across a 2.5-4 nm gap. The gap is made by removing an ALD sacrificial layer (carbon or Al2O3) and then sealed, like BEOL air-gaps or NASA's nanoscale vacuum-channel transistors, which work in air because the gap is far below the ~70 nm mean free path. The node is the gate of an IGZO or Si read transistor (2T-like gain cell), so the read is non-destructive. Writing uses field emission at a few V/nm (field enhancement 2-3 at edges); holding relies on the exponential non-linearity of tunnelling. Charge never passes through a solid dielectric, so there are no trap generation, SILC or charge-to-breakdown limits, the mechanisms that cap flash endurance at ~1e5. Low-work-function coatings (LaB6-class, 2.7 eV) cut write voltage, but even plain TiN (4.5 eV) works at 8 V.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 retention/refresh (refresh-free); A1 #1 (no capacitor: ~0.2 fF node); A1 #8 non-destructive read; endurance wall of charge-storage NVMs (A3 FeFET/flash kills).
ideas.step_change_claim: [SPECULATIVE] A non-volatile, refresh-free DRAM-class gain cell: retention 3.7e4 s (2.5 nm gap, 2.7 eV) to >1e8 s (3 nm), writes in 0.4-40 ns. Endurance is not set by oxide damage, with a target of >=1e12.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: FN: J = (1.54e-6 F2/phi) exp(-6.83e9 phi^1.5/F), with a 10x10 nm emission area and a 0.2 fF node. phi 2.7 eV, 3 nm gap, 6 V, beta 2: I = 0.47 uA -> 1 V in 0.43 ns. phi 4.5 eV (TiN), 4 nm gap, 8 V, beta 3: 24 nA -> 8.5 ns. Hold (Simmons low-voltage, 1 V across gap): phi 2.7 eV gives 6.6 s (2.0 nm), 3.7e4 s (2.5 nm), 2e8 s (3.0 nm); phi 4.5 eV gives 9e4 s (2 nm) and essentially unlimited at >=2.5 nm. Electrostatic pressure at 2.5 V/nm is 28 MPa, so the node must be anchored, not a free beam. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-09)

ideas.novelty: [SPECULATIVE] NEW combination: nanoscale vacuum-channel electronics (NASA Ames) + floating-gate gain cell. Nanogap memories based on atom migration exist, but a trap-free FN nanogap as the storage barrier of a DRAM-class gain cell was not found [UNVERIFIED].

(2) Field-emission instability: adsorbate diffusion, surface migration and emitter blunting change emission over cycles. (3) 6-8 V write drivers at tight pitch, plus charging of dielectric surfaces next to the gap.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Write-verify absorbs spread (as NAND does); use self-limiting ALD sacrificial layers for Å-level control. (2) Hermetic seal with getters, refractory emitters (W, TiN, HfC), and operation in emission regimes well below field-evaporation fields (6 vs ~50 V/nm for W). (3) Row-shared HV drivers like NAND; lateral geometry with no dielectric in the field path.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Lateral TiN nanogap floating-node test structures (3-4 nm ALD sacrificial release) coupled to an IGZO or Si sense FET, with at least two gap splits. Measure FN I-V, write time vs voltage, retention at 85-150 C, and cycling to 1e9-1e12 with emission-noise statistics. Budget ~$450k across a university nanofab plus a NASA Ames collaboration.
ideas.resource_angle: Uses only Ti, N, W, Si, O: no Hf, Ru or Ga. Non-volatile, so use-phase refresh energy disappears. Fabricated with ALD and release etch, no EUV.
ideas.us_buildable: Cornell CNF or Stanford SNF (nanogap release), NASA Ames (vacuum nanoelectronics), Sandia MESA (MEMS release and hermetic sealing).
ideas.triage_reason: Vacuum is a trap-free, wear-free tunnel barrier, so endurance escapes the charge-fluence rule. FN arithmetic (C0-3): with a 2.7 eV emitter, 0.1 fC writes in ps-ns at 6-8 V across 2.5-3 nm; with plain TiN (4.5 eV) it takes 0.16 us at 2.5 nm/8 V and 11 us at 3.0 nm, i.e. ~70x per 0.5 nm of gap. The idea therefore rests on (a) <=0.2 nm gap uniformity over 1e10 sealed cavities and (b) a stable low-work-function (<=3 eV) emitter surviving >=1e12 emission events; neither is shown.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when sealed 2.5-3 nm nanogaps show <=0.2 nm (1 sigma) gap spread and <=10% emission drift over 1e12 cycles at the write field.
ideas.claim_short: Non-volatile vacuum-gap floating node: ns writes at 6-8 V, trap-free barrier

ideas.name: Direct-tunnel charge-trap '3D AND' DRAM built with 3D-NAND tools
ideas.one_liner: Run the 3D-NAND tool set (one HAR etch through 64-256 tiers) but thin the tunnel layer to ~1.5-2 nm so cells program by low-field direct tunnelling in ns, hold for 1-100 s, and survive far more cycles; read cells in parallel (AND/NOR), not in series strings.
ideas.mechanism: Vertical channel holes (poly-Si or ALD IGZO/IGO) with vertical source/drain lines pass through stacked word planes (3D AND/NOR topology, as in SunRise 3D NOR and Macronix-style 3D AND). Gate stack: ~1.5-2 nm bandgap-engineered SiO2/SiON tunnel layer, SiN trap layer and Al2O3 blocking layer. Low-field direct tunnelling (few V) avoids the hot-carrier and FN damage that limits NAND endurance; retention falls to seconds-minutes, which is the trade: quasi-volatile. Each cell is read individually with ns-class parallel sensing on short vertical bitlines; refresh is 16-1,500x less frequent than DRAM.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 3D DRAM (uses a proven 3D process); A1 #4 capital/EUV (no EUV; NAND tools); A1 #3 refresh; A2 white space 1 (bits per capex dollar).
ideas.step_change_claim: 2.7-7.2x 1b density at 64-256 tiers on a NAND-class (EUV-free) line; refresh energy and time 16x (1 s) to 1,562x (100 s) lower.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Per-tier cell 0.030-0.045 um2, array efficiency 0.60: 64 tiers -> 1.20 Gb/mm2 (2.7x); 128 tiers -> 1.61-2.41 (3.6-5.4x); 256 tiers -> 3.21 (7.2x). Retention 1/10/100 s -> refresh x16/x156/x1,562 lower than 64 ms. With 10 s refresh, refresh cycles total 3.2e7 over 10 yr, so writes dominate endurance; the target is 1e10-1e12 with write-back caching. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-10)

ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Endurance of thin tunnel oxides at 1e10+ cycles is unproven; even low-field tunnelling generates traps over time. (2) Direct-tunnel write speed at low voltage may be µs, not 10-50 ns. (3) Vt distribution tails and retention tails at 85 C across 1e10 cells; vertical source/drain-line RC limits ns reads.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Bandgap-engineered tunnel stacks (BE-SONOS-like) and IGZO channels with no Si/SiO2 interface-state generation; accept 1e9-1e10 behind an SRAM/DRAM write cache. (2) Trade a slightly thicker barrier for retention, or use the hot-carrier assist of B1-20. (3) Short vertical lines (16-32 tiers per sense group), with ECC and retention-aware refresh (RAIDR-style).
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 4-16-tier test stacks with three tunnel-oxide splits at a university/300 mm partner (or single-tier planar charge-trap capacitors and transistors first). Measure program speed vs voltage, retention at 85 C, and endurance to 1e10 at 100 ns pulses. Budget ~$450k.
ideas.resource_angle: Re-uses NAND fabs (no EUV), including idle NAND capacity in a NAND downturn: a capital and supply-chain lever. SiN/SiO2 stacks avoid Ge (A2 flags the SiGe superlattice route at 6-38% of refined Ge).
ideas.us_buildable: Micron (Boise R&D; NAND expertise), NY CREATES Albany, SUNY Poly; university single-tier work at Penn State or NCSU.
ideas.triage_reason: Direct-tunnel charge-trap cells with seconds of retention exist (SunRise QV-NOR, NEO). Unproven: 1e10-1e12 writes through a 1.5-2 nm amorphous tunnel layer; the charge-fluence rule (C0-2) gives 1e3-1e5 writes at Q_BD 1-100 C/cm2 for 1 fC through 100 nm2, rescued only if ultrathin oxides at low field reach Q_BD >=1e5-1e7 C/cm2, or with a crystalline barrier.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a thin-tunnel charge-trap cell shows >=1e11 program/erase cycles at <=50 ns with >=1 s retention at 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Direct-tunnel charge-trap 3D AND on NAND tools: 2.7-7.2x density; refresh 16-1,562x less

ideas.name: Capacitive-NDRO ferroelectric gain cell for a read-mostly DRAM tier
ideas.one_liner: Read a ferroelectric capacitor's state from its small-signal capacitance (high vs low after imprint engineering) without switching it. Reads stop wearing the cell, refresh disappears, and DRAM-class read endurance is decoupled from the 1e7-class write endurance; a natural fit for inference-weight memory.
ideas.mechanism: An HZO (or Zr-rich) capacitor with asymmetric electrodes has a zero-bias capacitance that differs between its two polarization states (imec reports a capacitive window ~8.7 at 0 V). The capacitor is the coupling element of a read transistor gate (1T-1C_FE or 2T-nC with n<=4). A small read pulse (below coercive) on its plate couples more or less charge onto the gate, and the read transistor converts that to current. Reads are non-destructive and never switch polarization; writes are full switching pulses. The memory is non-volatile, so there is no refresh and no restore, and pages need not be activated wholesale. Small n is essential: capacitive coupling dilutes as 1/n.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh; A1 #8 destructive read and overfetch; A1 #5 data-movement energy for read-dominated AI workloads; A3 white space 2 (FE endurance).
ideas.step_change_claim: Refresh -> 0 and restore -> 0 for read-mostly data. Read endurance >1e11 (shown) vs ~1e7 write; read energy ~CV2 of a ~1.5 fF node (~0.1-0.4 fJ) instead of a 10 KB page restore (~5.9 pJ per useful bit random).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Node signal = V_read x dC/C x C_cap/(n C_cap + C_gate), with C_cap 1 fF, C_gate 0.5 fF, V_read 0.3 V. dC/C 0.5: n = 1 -> 100 mV, 2 -> 60 mV, 4 -> 33 mV, 8 -> 18 mV, 64 -> 2.3 mV (so 2T-64C capacitive read is infeasible). dC/C 1.0: n = 4 -> 67 mV. Writes in 10 yr at one rewrite per minute = 5.3e6 (1.9x margin vs 1e7); per hour 8.8e4 (114x margin). (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-11)

(2) Pair with a small DRAM/SRAM write buffer; target weights, embeddings and read-mostly KV pages. (3) Characterize disturb vs read amplitude; Zr-rich films reduce Hf.

absorbed_cards.name: Flat AlBN ferroelectric capacitor with non-destructive capacitive read
absorbed_cards.one_liner: Use Sc-free, Hf-free boron-aluminum nitride, whose remanent polarization (~125-136 uC/cm2) is ~5x hafnia's, to store a full DRAM bit's charge in a flat 20-40 nm capacitor with no height at all, and read it without switching.
absorbed_cards.mechanism: Sputter 5-10 nm wurtzite Al1-xBxN (x 0.02-0.15) at <=400 C on a planar landing pad: 2Pr*A for a 40x40 nm pad is ~4 fC (~26,000 e-), more than today's 1.3 um pillar delivers. Reads must not switch the film, so the state is read capacitively: the imprinted polarization gives different small-signal C (or a piezo/flexo-induced charge) for up and down states, sensed through a 2T gain cell on an oxide channel, so only writes wear the ferroelectric. Data are non-volatile: no refresh. A gain-cell or SRAM write buffer in front absorbs write traffic.
absorbed_cards.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 (removes the HAR capacitor), A1 #3 (no refresh), A2 (AlScN on 3D area would need ~13% of world Sc; HZO 14-41% of Hf).
absorbed_cards.step_change_claim: Zero capacitor height and zero refresh energy; 1-4 fC per bit from a planar 20-40 nm pad; Sc- and Hf-free. Gated by an endurance gap of ~1e5-1e9x.
absorbed_cards.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-06: 2Pr*A: Pr=130 uC/cm2, 20x20 nm -> 1.04 fC (6,492 e-); 40x40 nm -> 4.16 fC (25,968 e-); HZO-class Pr=25 at 20x20 nm -> 0.20 fC. Coercive voltage = Ec*t: 5.4 MV/cm x 5 nm = 2.7 V; with B+Sc co-alloys at 3 MV/cm, 5 nm -> 1.5 V. Endurance: >1e6 demonstrated vs ~3.4e15 needed for DRAM-class (3.4e9x) or 1.6e11 for a write-buffered tier (1.6e5x).

absorbed_cards.novelty: TWIST: AlBN ferroelectricity is known (Penn State 2021; Cornell MBE); using it as a flat, high-charge DRAM capacitor with non-destructive capacitive read behind a write buffer is a NEW combination.
absorbed_cards.show_stoppers: (1) Endurance: wurtzite ferroelectrics switch near breakdown; >1e6 shown vs 1e11-1e15 needed. (2) Coercive voltage of 1.5-2.7 V at 5 nm, and sub-5 nm switching is unproven [UNVERIFIED-PK]. (3) Leakage and wake-up in thin films (MBE AlBN reached only 15 uC/cm2 because of leakage).
absorbed_cards.revival_or_workaround: (1) Never switch on read (capacitive read); write buffer + wear-levelling so a cell sees <=1 write/ms; B co-alloying is reported to improve endurance, so map the trend toward 1e10+. (2) B+Sc co-alloys at ~3 MV/cm, or minor-loop/partial switching at lower voltage. (3) N-rich, H-free sputtering and textured templates.
absorbed_cards.million_dollar_demo: 12-15 months, ~$250k: sputtered AlBN MFM capacitors scaled from 20 to 5 nm; Pr, Ec, 10-100 ns pulse endurance, 125 C retention, and the capacitive read margin (C asymmetry up vs down) on 40-200 nm pads. Kill test: no path to >=1e10 cycles at <=2 V.
absorbed_cards.resource_angle: Al, B and N are among the most abundant inputs; replaces Sc (13% of world supply at 3D scale) and Hf. Non-volatility removes refresh energy in use, the largest lifetime energy term (A2: ~16x fab energy).
absorbed_cards.us_buildable: Penn State MRI (State College PA); Penn Singh Center (Philadelphia, AlScN groups); Cornell (MBE AlBN); Sandia CINT.

ideas.triage_reason: imec showed capacitive NDRO of a ferroelectric capacitor (IEDM 2023) with >1e11 reads, so the read physics is demonstrated; write endurance (HZO ~1e7-1e11) confines it to read-mostly tiers. Merged B2-06 (flat AlBN FE capacitor, also read capacitively through a 2T gain cell): its ~5x larger Pr does not enter a capacitive read (the signal is the up/down C asymmetry, ~0.002-0.005 fF on a 20-40 nm pad at k~11, readable only through a gain-cell gate), so AlBN's real benefits are a Sc/Hf-free flat film; its gap is write endurance (best 2025 wurtzite report >1e10 cycles in sub-50 nm AlScN, preprint, vs the 1.6e11 a write-buffered tier needs).
ideas.revival_condition: Alive for HZO. The AlBN variant is ALIVE-SPECULATIVE until a wurtzite FE shows >=1.6e11 cycles at <=2 V. Kill test for both: imprint-window drift >50% over 1 day at 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Capacitive non-destructive FE read: refresh/restore -> 0 for read-mostly data (read endurance >1e11)
dead_subclaims: B2-06: 1-4 fC of 2Pr*A is available only to a switching (destructive) read, not to the capacitive read the card specifies

ideas.name: Sliding-ferroelectric 2D gain channel (fatigue-free polarization)
ideas.one_liner: Use interlayer-sliding ferroelectricity (bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2) as the storage mechanism of a 1T gain cell. Switching moves no ions, so the fatigue and wake-up that kill hafnia FE endurance may not exist: >1e11 ns cycles have been shown.
ideas.mechanism: In AB/BA-stacked bilayers, an out-of-plane polarization flips when one layer slides by a fraction of a lattice constant. No ions move, so there is no oxygen-vacancy migration and no charged-defect build-up. A semiconducting 3R-MoS2 bilayer can serve as both channel and ferroelectric, or a bilayer-hBN gate ferroelectric can sit on a MoS2/IGZO channel. Polarization ~0.7 uC/cm2 (~4e12 e/cm2) shifts Vt by 0.16-0.30 V per state at EOT 0.8-1.5 nm, a 0.3-0.6 V window. The cell is non-volatile with a non-destructive gain read, written at <1 V in ns.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh; A3 kill of FeFET for endurance (window collapse after 1e4-1e6 cycles); A1 #10 voltage floor.
ideas.step_change_claim: [SPECULATIVE at array scale] A ferroelectric 1T DRAM-class cell with endurance on a path to >=1e12-1e15 (1e11 shown), zero refresh, and sub-1 V ns writes: closes the 1e8x endurance gap that kills hafnia FeFETs.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: P_eff ~0.68 uC/cm2 (2.25 pC/m dipole / 0.33 nm) [ESTIMATE] = 4.2e12 e/cm2. Vt shift = P/C_gate: EOT 0.8/1.0/1.5 nm -> 0.16/0.20/0.30 V per state (window 0.32/0.39/0.59 V). Evidence: 3R-MoS2 no fatigue after 1e6 cycles (ms pulses); bilayer-BN FeFET >1e11 cycles, ns. A 4F2 1T cell at F = 20 nm = 0.30 Gb/mm2 per layer. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-12)

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known: sliding ferroelectrics (2021-2024 Science papers) are a physics discovery, and memory demonstrations are single devices. Positioning them as a DRAM-class gain cell with an endurance target of 1e15 is open.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Wafer-scale growth with controlled rhombohedral/AB stacking at BEOL temperatures. (2) Domain size: sliding domain walls are wide solitons, and a 20 nm cell may sit below the minimum stable domain. (3) Retention at 85-125 C, since sliding barriers are small (meV per formula unit).
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) The Penn State 2DCC MOCVD wafer program and transfer-free epitaxy on sapphire, then bonded transfer. (2) Measure the minimum switchable area; if it exceeds ~50 nm, use 2-bit cells at a larger pitch or a vertical channel. (3) Interlayer pinning and electrostatic built-in bias; screen hBN vs TMD vs In2Se3 variants.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Exfoliated and CVD bilayer devices (hBN/MoS2) scaled from 1 um down to 50 nm. Measure endurance at 10 ns pulses to 1e12, retention vs temperature, and the window vs size. Budget ~$300k, mostly people and cryo/hot probe time at shared facilities.
ideas.resource_angle: Mo, S, B, N: no Hf, no Ga. Sub-1 V operation cuts energy.
ideas.us_buildable: Penn State 2D Crystal Consortium (NSF MIP) for wafers, Cornell CNF, Columbia, MIT.nano.
ideas.triage_reason: Sliding ferroelectricity is real at room temperature and moves no ions, so hafnia's fatigue mechanisms may be absent (1e11 claimed, unattributed). Unproven: stable bistable domains in a <=20-50 nm cell when sliding domain walls are wide solitons; retention at 85-125 C with meV-per-unit-cell barriers; wafer-scale stacking-order control at BEOL temperature.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a <=50 nm sliding-FE gain cell shows >=1e12 ns cycles and >=1 s retention at 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Sliding-ferroelectric 2D gain cell: ion-free switching, endurance path to 1e12-1e15

ideas.name: Lithium-niobate-on-insulator conductive-domain-wall memory
ideas.one_liner: Store a bit as the presence or absence of a conductive charged domain wall between two nano-electrodes in single-crystal LNOI (the photonics-industry wafer). Reads are non-destructive at low voltage; writes switch at ~0.4-1 V for 20-50 nm gaps.
ideas.mechanism: Thin-film LiNbO3 bonded on SiO2/Si (LNOI) is single-crystal. Applying a field across two in-plane electrodes inverts a nano-domain, creating a head-to-head charged wall that conducts (giant DW conductivity); removing it erases. A small read voltage senses wall current without moving the wall (NDRO, ~1e3 on/off). Embedded selectors give >1e6 selectivity for crosspoint arrays. Being a single crystal, LN has no grain boundaries or oxygen-vacancy-rich interlayers, the source of hafnia's wake-up/fatigue; its endurance under ns pulses is the open question.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh (non-volatile); A1 #8 destructive read; A3 FE endurance concerns.
ideas.step_change_claim: Non-volatile NDRO 2-terminal cell at 0.4-1 V. Density is NOT the step: 0.2x 1b per layer at F = 40 nm, 0.79x with 4 bonded layers. The claim is endurance and energy (no refresh, no restore), still to be proven.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Switching voltage = E_c x gap with E_c ~21 V/um (congruent LN [ESTIMATE]): 20/50/100 nm gaps -> 0.42/1.05/2.1 V. Density: 4F2 crosspoint at F = 40 nm = 0.09 Gb/mm2 (0.20x 1b); 4 bonded layers 0.35 (0.79x); F = 20 nm single layer 0.35 (0.79x). (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-13)

ideas.novelty: KNOWN (Fudan A.Q. Jiang group, Queen's Belfast, Dresden/Fraunhofer DW memories). TWIST: use photonics LNOI wafers and a DRAM-class endurance target.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) No public ns-pulse endurance data at 1e12+. (2) Single-crystal LN cannot be deposited monolithically; every layer is a bonded wafer, which caps 3D density. (3) DW current variability and wall pinning at <30 nm.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Measure first; LN's lack of vacancy-mediated fatigue makes it a credible bet. (2) Accept as a non-volatile cache or near-logic tier where density matters less; one bonded LNOI layer on logic. (3) Mg-doped LN lowers E_c and pinning.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Commercial LNOI coupons; e-beam patterned 20-100 nm gap electrodes. Measure write voltage, read current, retention at 85 C, and 10 ns-pulse endurance to 1e12. Budget ~$250k.
ideas.resource_angle: Li and Nb, not chokepoints; no Hf. LNOI wafer supply is concentrated in a few suppliers [UNVERIFIED].
ideas.us_buildable: Harvard CNS and Cornell CNF (LNOI patterning), Penn Singh Center; U.S. LNOI photonics startups as wafer partners [UNVERIFIED].
ideas.triage_reason: Conductive domain-wall memories in LiNbO3 are demonstrated, and LN's coercive field (~21 V/um, congruent) gives ~0.4 V across a 20 nm gap, consistent with the card. Unproven: ns-pulse endurance >=1e12 (no data) and DW-current uniformity below 30 nm. Bonded single-crystal layers cap density (0.2-0.79x 1b) but that is not a physics kill.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when 20-50 nm LNOI DW cells show >=1e12 cycles at 10 ns with <=2x DW-current spread.
ideas.claim_short: LNOI conductive-domain-wall NDRO cell at 0.4-1 V (energy/endurance play, not density)

ideas.name: VCMA crosspoint MRAM with deliberately relaxed (refreshed) retention
ideas.one_liner: Write MTJs with voltage (VCMA precessional switching, 6-20 fJ) in a selector crosspoint stacked 4 decks high, and size the magnetic barrier for ~1 s refresh instead of 10 years; that cuts the needed barrier ~31% and lets the free layer shrink.
ideas.mechanism: Each crosspoint is an OTS selector plus a perpendicular CoFeB/MgO MTJ with a high VCMA coefficient. A ~0.5-1 ns voltage pulse lowers the anisotropy so the free layer precesses half a turn, with no write current through a transistor, so there is no access transistor and the cell is 4F2. Thermal stability Delta is chosen for refreshed operation (Delta ~44-48 for 1 s to 1 min, vs ~64 for 10-year non-volatility), allowing a smaller or thinner free layer and lower write voltage. A 'refresh' is a TMR read plus conditional rewrite, done rarely. Four BEOL decks stack over CMOS.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh energy; A1 #4 density without litho shrink (decks); A1 #9 row hammer (magnetic bits have no charge-injection disturb); A3 MRAM density kill (STT 16x 1b area).
ideas.step_change_claim: 2.9x 1b density (4 decks, F = 20 nm) or 1.3x (F = 30 nm, no EUV); write energy 6-20 fJ vs a 46 fJ refresh plus pJ-class activation; refresh 15x+ less frequent than DRAM.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Delta >= ln(N t/tau0) with N = 1.7e10 and tau0 = 1 ns: 1 s -> 44.3; 1 min -> 48.4; 10 yr -> 63.8 kT, so relaxing to 1 s cuts Delta by 31%. Density: 4F2 x 1 deck at F = 20 nm = 0.32 Gb/mm2 (0.72x); 4 decks 1.29 (2.9x); 4 decks at F = 30 nm 0.58 (1.3x). (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-14)

evidence.title: imec voltage-MRAM breakthroughs (eeNews Europe 2020)
evidence.shows: VCMA: 20 fJ, 1.1 GHz, >1e10 cycles, field-free (CROSS-REF A3)

evidence.title: Spintec bidirectional VCMA switching
evidence.shows: 6 fJ/bit at 0.5 ns (CROSS-REF A3)

ideas.novelty: TWIST: VCMA MRAM is known (imec, UCLA lineage, Spintec); relaxed-retention STT for caches is known. The combination of selector crosspoint VCMA, multi-deck stacking and DRAM-style refresh as a DRAM replacement is an underexplored corner (A3 white space 6).
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Precessional write-error rate and pulse-timing precision across 1e10 cells (needs ~1e-9 after ECC). (2) VCMA coefficient too low at 20 nm for <=1 V writes with Delta ~45. (3) MgO endurance (~1e10 shown) and selector half-select leakage.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Write-verify-retry and a VCMA+STT assist; ECC with 2-error correction. (2) Heavy-metal and oxide interface engineering (Ir, Hf insertion, high-k caps); the target coefficient is >300 fJ/Vm. (3) Low-voltage VCMA writes stress MgO far less than STT.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: MTJ stacks with VCMA-optimised interfaces at a U.S. magnetics lab, plus 1S1MTJ crosspoint 8x8 arrays. Measure WER vs pulse width, Delta vs size at 85 C, endurance. Budget ~$500k (sputter-tool time is the main cost).
ideas.resource_angle: Co, Fe, B, Mg, Pt/Ir/W in nm films: small quantities, but Pt/Ir/Ru group exposure exists. No EUV at F = 30 nm with 4 decks.
ideas.us_buildable: UMN Minnesota Nano Center, UCLA, NIST/CHiPS magnetics; SkyWater (MN) BEOL integration later.
ideas.triage_reason: VCMA precessional switching at 6-20 fJ is demonstrated, and relaxing retention to ~1 s cuts the needed barrier from ~64-73 kT to ~35-44 kT with ECC (B5-00 ledger). Unproven: a VCMA coefficient >=300 fJ/Vm with high TMR at 20 nm (typical CoFeB/MgO ~30-100), a precessional write-error rate ~1e-9 across 1e10 cells, and MgO endurance beyond ~1e10.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a 20-30 nm VCMA MTJ shows <=1 V writes, raw WER <=1e-6, xi >=300 fJ/Vm and >=1e12 cycles.
ideas.claim_short: VCMA crosspoint MRAM, 4 decks, 1 s retention: 2.9x 1b density, 6-20 fJ writes

ideas.name: Shared-rail SOT tier on hot logic (4 MTJs per write rail)
ideas.one_liner: Put a non-volatile SOT-MRAM tier directly on logic, sharing each spin-Hall write rail among 4 MTJs: SRAM-class speed and >1e15 endurance at 2-2.6x SRAM macro density, with no refresh at 125 C.
ideas.mechanism: A W/Ta (or field-free FM/Ta) spin-orbit rail carries the write current; four MTJs sit on it, selected by per-MTJ voltage biasing (VCMA-assisted) or by staggered critical currents along the track. One write transistor and per-MTJ read selects are shared. Thermal stability is designed for 125 C junction temperatures, so data persist where Si DRAM would need ~4 ms refresh. Reads use TMR; writes take <10 ns at <100 fJ. This is not a commodity-density play; it attacks the memory-on-logic bottleneck.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #5 interface/data-movement energy (bits within 100 um of compute) and its thermal blocker; A1 #6 HBM tax for on-package capacity.
ideas.step_change_claim: 2.2-2.6x SRAM macro density (0.086-0.10 Gb/mm2 vs ~0.04) with zero standby/refresh at 125 C and >1e15 cycles; 0.19-0.23x 1b density (honest: it does not beat DRAM density).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: F = 20 nm: 1 MTJ per 30F2 group -> 12,000 nm2/bit -> 0.043 Gb/mm2; 4 MTJ per 60F2 -> 6,000 nm2/bit -> 0.086 Gb/mm2 (2.2x N2 SRAM ~0.04 [A1]); 8 MTJ per 100F2 -> 0.104 (2.6x). More than 4 MTJs per rail runs into IR-drop and WER limits per the literature. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-15)

ideas.novelty: KNOWN: shared-rail and NAND-like SOT architectures (academic 2019-2022, patents). TWIST: framing it as a 125 C memory-on-logic tier to replace part of HBM capacity, not as cache.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) IR drop and write disturb on shared rails beyond 4 MTJs. (2) Field-free switching at small CD. (3) Thermal stability at 125 C for small MTJs while keeping write current low.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Stop at 4 per rail; use VCMA assist for selectivity. (2) imec's field-free FM/Ta approach. (3) Accept Delta ~60 at 125 C with slightly larger MTJs (density hit ~1.3x).
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 4-MTJ rail test structures through a university magnetics line or a foundry MRAM shuttle, tested at 125 C for WER, disturb and retention. Budget ~$400k.
ideas.resource_angle: Cuts the HBM wafer tax (A1: ~3x wafer per bit) for capacity placed on logic. Uses W (China-concentrated), Pt/Ta in small amounts.
ideas.us_buildable: UMN, NIST; GlobalFoundries (Malta) eMRAM know-how; SkyWater BEOL.
ideas.triage_reason: SOT-MRAM above 1e15 cycles at <100 fJ is demonstrated (imec) and shared-rail architectures are published; field-free switching and IR drop on 4-MTJ rails are engineering. Honest scope: SRAM-replacement density (0.19-0.23x 1b), not DRAM density.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: write disturb on unselected MTJs of a shared rail >1e-9 per write at 125 C.
ideas.claim_short: Shared-rail SOT tier on logic: 2.2-2.6x SRAM density, >1e15 cycles, zero standby at 125 C

ideas.name: Protonic gain cell (H+ in WO3 behind a PSG electrolyte)
ideas.one_liner: Store the bit as the proton content of a WO3 channel, written in ns through a phosphosilicate-glass proton electrolyte at ~1 V/nm (the MIT protonic resistor) and read non-destructively as channel conductance: an analog, non-volatile, multi-level gain cell made from CMOS-native materials.
ideas.mechanism: Three terminals: a WO3 channel between source and drain; a nanoporous PSG electrolyte (2-5 nm) above it; a Pd (or PdHx) gate that serves as the proton reservoir. A gate pulse at ~1 V/nm drives H+ into or out of WO3 in ns; each inserted proton is charge-compensated by an electron, which raises channel conductance. At read voltages the field is too low to move protons, so the state is non-volatile and the read is non-destructive. Multi-level storage is natural (analog conductance). The 'protonic nano-supercapacitor stub' variant, which uses the same chemistry as a 2-terminal capacitor holding ~18x today's charge per area, is rejected: its charge cannot be extracted at low field in ns (see notes).
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh (non-volatile); A1 #1 (no capacitor); A1 #8 non-destructive read; A1 #4 density via multi-level.
ideas.step_change_claim: Non-volatile 2-4 b/cell gain cell with 5 ns writes; refresh -> 0. Density per tier similar to a 2T0C (~10F2) but multiplied by bits per cell. Unproven endurance.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Write voltage = 1 V/nm x PSG thickness: 2/5/10 nm -> 2/5/10 V. Charge density of WO3 at dx = 0.1 H/W in 2 nm: 60 uC/cm2 = 18x today's 3.3 uC/cm2 wall signal (why the capacitor version is tempting); but extraction needs the same ~1 V/nm, so it fails as a fast capacitor. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-16)

evidence.title: Nanosecond protonic programmable resistors (Onen et al., Science 2022)
evidence.shows: WO3/PSG/Pd, ~1 V/nm, ns programming, CMOS-native materials (via search snippet)

evidence.title: MIT protonic programmable resistor press release (ScienceDaily 2022-07-28)
evidence.shows: PSG electrolyte ~1e6x faster than the team's previous device; room temperature (press claim, via search snippet)

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known (MIT del Alamo/Li/Yildiz protonic resistors for analog AI; IBM ECRAM lineage). Repurposing as a digital multi-level DRAM-class gain cell is new framing.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Hydrogen is the enemy of oxide and Si transistors (H is a donor in IGZO and drives PBTI), so a proton reservoir next to the access device is an integration hazard. (2) Endurance at 1e12+ ns cycles is unknown (WO3 lattice strain, PSG degradation). (3) 2-5 V writes and the ion-motion energy per write.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Hermetic H barriers (Al2O3, SiN) around each cell; physically separate tiers. (2) Measure; if <1e10, target a read-mostly tier (like B1-11). (3) Thinner PSG (2 nm) brings writes to ~2 V.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Collaborate with the MIT protonic team: single devices scaled to 50 nm, measuring 10 ns write endurance to 1e10-1e12, retention at 85 C, and H outdiffusion into a neighbouring IGZO TFT. Budget ~$300k.
ideas.resource_angle: W, P, Si, O, Pd (small): Pd is a precious metal (Russia/South Africa concentrated). No Hf.
ideas.us_buildable: MIT.nano, Harvard CNS, Sandia (ECRAM work).
ideas.triage_reason: ns proton motion through PSG at ~1 V/nm is demonstrated (MIT). Unproven: >=1e12 cycles of faradaic proton insertion into WO3 (battery-class lattice chemistry; analog-synapse data are ~1e5-1e8 pulses), and keeping mobile H away from IGZO, where hydrogen is a donor.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a WO3/PSG cell shows >=1e12 5 ns cycles with <=10% window loss and no Vt shift in an adjacent IGZO FET at 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Protonic WO3 gain cell: non-volatile 2-4 b/cell, 5 ns writes

ideas.name: Redox-molecule pseudocapacitor with natural multi-level plateaus (ZettaCore revival)
ideas.one_liner: Replace the dielectric in a short pillar with a monolayer of redox molecules (porphyrins) behind a solid nano-electrolyte. Each molecule stores one electron per discrete oxidation state, giving 2.4-4.9x today's charge per area and built-in voltage plateaus for 2 bits/cell.
ideas.mechanism: ZettaCore's cell is a standard DRAM 1T cell whose capacitor is replaced by a porphyrin self-assembled monolayer between electrodes, an electrochemical cell. Charge is held in the molecules' discrete redox states, which appear at fixed potentials (e.g., +0.5 and +0.8 V), so voltage levels quantize naturally: multi-level storage without analog trimming. Retention of minutes was reported, vs tens of ms for DRAM. The twist: tether the SAM to a TiN pillar wall, fill the gap with an ALD-compatible solid ion conductor (or confined ionic liquid) for counter-charge, and read through an IGZO access device with 3-level sensing.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor charge wall; A1 #4 density via levels; A1 #3 retention (minutes).
ideas.step_change_claim: 2.4-4.9x signal charge per area -> pillar 1,300 -> 270-540 nm at equal charge per state; 1.6-2 bits/cell from discrete plateaus -> up to ~2x density at the same cell.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Molecule footprint 1-2 nm2 -> 5e13-1e14 /cm2 -> 8-16 uC/cm2 per redox state = 2.4-4.9x today's 3.3 uC/cm2. Pillar for 2.84 fC per state: 535-267 nm. 2-3 oxidation states (plus neutral) -> log2(3-4) = 1.6-2.0 bits/cell. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-17)

ideas.novelty: KNOWN (ZettaCore; NCSU Bocian/Lindsey/Misra; funded by DARPA Moletronics). TWIST: solid-state electrolyte in a stub pillar plus an oxide access device and MLC sensing.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) The counter-ion electrolyte must be solid, nm-thin, and survive 400 C BEOL. (2) Electron-transfer and ion-motion rates may not support 10-50 ns reads and writes. (3) Molecular stability over 1e12-1e15 redox cycles at 85 C.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Li/Na-free solid proton or anion conductors (ALD LiPON analogues avoided); add molecules post-BEOL as a last-step module. (2) Short tethers, conjugated linkers, and use only at 50-100 ns latency tiers. (3) Accelerated cycling; choose porphyrin/ferrocene families with known robustness.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Molecules on TiN/ITO pillar arrays with solid electrolytes. Measure fast cyclic voltammetry, ns-to-us pulsed charge, plateau separation, retention and cycling at 85 C. Budget ~$350k.
ideas.resource_angle: C, H, N plus a central metal (Zn/Co): abundant. Shorter pillars cut etch capital. Electrolyte chemistry may add PFAS-like risk if fluorinated salts are used (avoid them).
ideas.us_buildable: NCSU (original team region) and the NCSU Nanofab, Duke SMIF, UC Riverside.
ideas.triage_reason: Porphyrin monolayers at ~1e-10 mol/cm2 store ~10 uC/cm2 per redox state (~3x the 3.3 uC/cm2 linear signal) and reportedly survived 400 C and ~1e12 cycles in liquid electrolyte [UNVERIFIED-PK, ZettaCore/NCSU era]. Unproven: a nm-thin solid counter-ion electrolyte supporting >=1e8 s^-1 redox at 85 C; tethered-molecule electron transfer is typically us-class.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a solid-electrolyte porphyrin stub delivers >=50% of its charge in a 50 ns pulse and survives >=1e12 cycles at 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Redox-molecule pseudocapacitor stub: 2.4-4.9x charge/area, 2 b/cell plateaus

ideas.name: NEMS relay access switch: zero-GIDL DRAM cell
ideas.one_liner: Replace the access transistor with a nano-electromechanical relay whose open state has an air gap, so off-current is essentially zero. Today's 5.4 fF capacitor then holds for 10-100 s (dielectric-limited), the wordline drops from 2.9 V to ~1 V, and there is no floating body to hammer.
ideas.mechanism: A vertical TiN/W cantilever or clamped beam over each storage node is pulled in by the wordline electrode, closing a contact between bitline and capacitor; open, an air or vacuum gap isolates the node. Leakage then is only the capacitor dielectric's own (~1e-8-1e-7 A/cm2). Switching is abrupt (effectively 0 mV/dec), so the wordline needs only the pull-in voltage (~1 V) with no charge pump. A 100-200 nm beam resonates at 0.4-1.2 GHz, giving ~0.5-1.5 ns mechanical switching. Contacts switch only fC of charge at uA levels, far gentler than RF-MEMS hot switching.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 leakage tail/refresh; A1 #10 wordline voltage (pump energy); A1 #9 row hammer (no charge injection from neighbour wordlines).
ideas.step_change_claim: Refresh 150-1,500x less frequent (10-100 s retention with today's capacitor); wordline energy ~0.06x (1 V unpumped vs 2.9 V pumped); hammer-immune by construction.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Dielectric leakage 1e-8/1e-7 A/cm2 on the 8.6e-10 cm2 pillar wall -> 8.6/86 aA -> retention 97/10 s (155 mV droop on 5.4 fF). Cantilever 200x10 nm (E 250 GPa, rho 3200) -> f0 0.36 GHz -> ~1.4 ns; 100x8 nm -> 1.15 GHz -> ~0.44 ns. Contact charge 2.7 fC per access. Wordline energy ratio (1/2.9)^2 x 0.45/0.95 = 0.06. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-18)

ideas.novelty: KNOWN (IBM NEM-DRAM patent; NEM eDRAM at DATE 2020). TWIST: a vertical relay in a 4-6F2 pillar, with an explicit cold-switching argument for contact endurance.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Contact endurance at 1e12-1e15 cycles is unmeasured (RF-MEMS ~1e12 by analogy). (2) Stiction and adhesion at nm contacts, and contact resistance drift. (3) Fabricating a released mechanical structure per cell at 20-30 nm pitch, with yield at 1e10.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Cycle relays at 100 MHz (1e12 cycles in ~3 h) with fF loads; refractory contacts (W, Ru-free carbides). (2) Anti-stiction monolayers, sealed vacuum cavities. (3) Start at a relaxed pitch for an eDRAM/near-logic tier, where retention and hammer immunity matter more than density.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Lateral TiN relays with fF loads at a university nanofab. Measure pull-in voltage, switching time, contact resistance, and 1e12-cycle endurance at 85 C. Then a 1R1C retention demo. Budget ~$350k.
ideas.resource_angle: Ti, N, W: no Hf/Ga/Ru. Removes wordline charge pumps (energy). Release etch adds process but no EUV.
ideas.us_buildable: UC Berkeley Marvell Nanolab (NEM relay lineage), Sandia MESA, Cornell CNF.
ideas.triage_reason: An open vacuum/air gap gives essentially zero off-current, so retention becomes dielectric-limited: sound. Unproven: nm-contact endurance of 1e13-1e15 cold-switched cycles (best relay data ~1e9-1e11), adhesion and contact-resistance drift, and a released relay inside a 4-6F2 pillar.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when <=50 nm relays cycle >=1e13 times at fF loads with contact-resistance drift <2x.
ideas.claim_short: NEMS relay access switch: zero GIDL, 10-100 s retention with today's capacitor, hammer-immune

ideas.name: NbO2 Mott threshold switch as an in-stack local sense element
ideas.one_liner: Use the abrupt, regenerative insulator-to-metal threshold switching of NbO2 as a one-device comparator per 64-cell local bitline, built in the BEOL cell stack. Short bitlines (Cs needed 1.2 fF, VARY ~0.4 V) then become possible without silicon sense amps under every bitline.
ideas.mechanism: A ~10-20 nm NbO2 device biased just below its threshold voltage sits on each local bitline segment. A '1' signal (~200 mV on a 64-cell segment) tips it over threshold; Joule heating drives the Mott transition (~1080 K locally) and the device snaps to a low-resistance state, producing a large current spike that a shared global sense line or latch detects. A '0' leaves it insulating. The device is a regenerative, abrupt, non-linear element only ~20 nm across, stackable in the cell tiers. Mott insulators cannot isolate a storage node (their off-state conductivity is many orders too high), so this card uses the transition only for sensing.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4/#7 (sense-amp area and array efficiency for short bitlines); A1 #1 via short bitlines; A1 #10 voltage floor; A1 #2 3D (local sensing every N tiers).
ideas.step_change_claim: [SPECULATIVE] Enables 64-cell local bitlines inside a 3D/BEOL stack: Cs need drops 5.4 -> ~1.2 fF and VARY to ~0.4 V (array energy ~16x lower per A1), without 8x more silicon sense amps.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Thermal energy to heat a 10/20 nm NbO2 cube from 85 C to the IMT (C_v 3 J/cm3K): 2.2/17 fJ (x3-10 with losses). Threshold sigma 1/2/5% of 1.0 V = 10/20/50 mV vs a 214 mV 1-bit signal on a 64-cell bitline: OK at <=2-5% sigma, hopeless at 512 cells (71 mV). (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-19)

evidence.title: Vollrath: DRAM signal margin (charge-sharing physics)
evidence.shows: Signal = (Vcell - VBLEQ) Cs/(Cs+Cbl); shorter bitlines raise signal (CROSS-REF A1)

evidence.title: Cbl = per-cell contribution x cell count + SA contribution (US 12,106,797)
evidence.shows: Bitline capacitance scales with cells per bitline (CROSS-REF A1)

ideas.novelty: [SPECULATIVE] NEW use: NbO2 threshold switches are known as selectors and oscillators (HP Labs lineage) [UNVERIFIED: no URL this session]; as a DRAM local sense element, no prior was found.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device threshold variation (often several %) and its strong ambient-temperature dependence. (2) Energy per sense (~10-100 fJ with losses) may exceed a CMOS sense amp's. (3) Endurance of threshold switching at 1e12-1e15 events and thermal crosstalk between neighbours.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Self-referenced two-step sensing (sense, write reference, sense) with per-device calibration; temperature-tracking bias. (2) Use only for segment select and pre-amplification, with a shared CMOS latch. (3) If it fails, fall back to oxide-TFT sense amps in BEOL.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Sputtered NbOx devices (10-50 nm) at a university fab. Measure threshold distributions vs temperature and pulse width, energy per event and endurance; then connect them to IGZO 1T1C test segments. Budget ~$300k.
ideas.resource_angle: Nb is concentrated (Brazil ~90%) but used in tiny amounts. Moves sensing out of costly front-end silicon area.
ideas.us_buildable: Sandia MESA, Penn State, Purdue Birck.
ideas.triage_reason: A Mott threshold switch can act as a regenerative comparator, so the capacitor-shrink claim (Cs 5.4 -> ~1.2 fF) survives if threshold sigma is <=~10 mV. The energy claim does not: NbO2 switches by Joule heating to ~1,080 K, so even a 10 nm core needs >=2.2 fJ (20 nm: 17 fJ) with zero losses (C0-5), above the 1.3 fJ bitline CV^2 (8 fF, 0.4 V) it was meant to enable. Thermal threshold noise is small (0.77 K rms in a 10 nm core), so variability is a materials question.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when threshold switches show <=10 mV cycle-to-cycle and <=20 mV device-to-device sigma at 85 C over 1e12 events. The energy claim revives only with a non-thermal threshold mechanism.
ideas.claim_short: NbO2 threshold switch as a one-device local sense amp per 64-cell bitline
dead_subclaims: ~16x array-energy reduction: the thermal switching floor (>=2-17 fJ per decision) exceeds the bitline energy saved

ideas.name: 2D-barrier quasi-volatile 1T cell (seconds-to-minutes retention traded for endurance)
ideas.one_liner: Take Fudan's 2D-enhanced fast charge-injection memories (400 ps program, non-volatile) and deliberately thin the hBN barrier, trading 10-year retention for 10-100 s. Writes then run at lower field and should damage the stack far less, giving a 1T 4F2 cell with 156-1,560x less refresh.
ideas.mechanism: A graphene or MoS2 channel sits over an hBN tunnel barrier (2-4 layers) and a floating gate or charge-storage layer (HfO2/Al2O3 or graphene). Fudan's PoX showed 2D-enhanced hot-carrier injection programming in 400 ps at 5 V, with 5.5e6 cycles. Fudan's 2D semi-floating gate showed 10 s retention with ~15 ns writes. The twist is to tune barrier thickness and injection mechanism (direct tunnelling vs hot-carrier) for a DRAM point: retention 10-100 s at 85 C, writes <=10 ns at ~2-3 V, and endurance as the optimisation target rather than retention. The read is non-destructive (gain cell). The cell is 1T, 4F2, BEOL-stackable if 2D films grow on wafers.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh; A1 #1 no capacitor; A1 #8 non-destructive read.
ideas.step_change_claim: Refresh 156x (10 s) to 1,562x (100 s) less frequent; 1T 4F2 at F = 20 nm = 0.30 Gb/mm2 per layer (0.67x 1b), multiplied by layers or bits per cell. Endurance must rise 1.8e5x to reach 1e12.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Retention 10/100 s vs 64 ms -> x156/x1,562 refresh reduction. Endurance gap: 1e12/5.5e6 = 1.8e5x; to 1e15, 1.8e8x. 4F2 at F = 20 nm = 0.30 Gb/mm2/tier. (research/models/B1_cellphysics_estimates.py B1-20)
