ideas.novelty: TWIST on known (Fudan PoX 2025, 2D SFG 2018): retargeting from flash/SRAM replacement toward a DRAM endurance/retention point.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) The endurance gap (1.8e5-1.8e8x) may be intrinsic to charge injection through any barrier. (2) Wafer-scale 2D growth and transfer at BEOL temperature with low defectivity. (3) Vt variability of 2D devices for reliable sensing.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Direct tunnelling only (no hot carriers) through atomically perfect hBN, which has no dangling-bond trap generation sites; measure endurance vs barrier thickness. (2) Penn State 2DCC MOCVD wafers; Fudan-style direct growth on CMOS (94% yield shown). (3) Write-verify, 1 b/cell.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: hBN-barrier-thickness splits (2/3/4 layers) on MoS2 or graphene FETs with HfO2 storage. Measure retention at 85 C vs write energy, and endurance at 10 ns writes to 1e12. Budget ~$300k.
ideas.resource_angle: Mo, S, B, N, C: no Hf (if graphene FG), no Ga. Lower write voltage cuts energy.
ideas.us_buildable: Penn State 2DCC, Columbia, MIT.nano, Cornell CNF.
ideas.triage_reason: Fudan's 2D fast charge-injection cells (400 ps program) are real, and trading ~20-30 kT of retention barrier for a lower write field is sound (B5-00). Unproven: the 1.8e5-1.8e8x endurance gap. Under the charge-fluence rule only a crystalline (hBN) barrier with direct tunnelling can plausibly carry 1e12 writes, and no such data exist (no RTD-class lifetime-vs-fluence data turned up either).
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when an hBN-barrier cell shows >=1e12 cycles at <=10 ns with >=10 s retention at 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: 2D-barrier quasi-volatile 1T: 10-100 s retention traded for endurance; refresh 156-1,562x less

ideas.name: AAO-Cap: self-ordered anodic-alumina capacitor mold
ideas.one_liner: Grow the DRAM capacitor holes by anodizing an aluminum film whose pores self-organize, imprint-registered to the transistors, instead of plasma-etching 60:1 holes in SiO2 with fluorocarbons.
ideas.mechanism: Sputter a 2.5-3 um Al film over the access-transistor array and its TiN/W landing pads. Nanoimprint shallow pits registered to the pads (Masuda pretexturing), then anodize at ~15-20 V in sulfuric/oxalic acid: pores nucleate at the pits and grow straight down at aspect ratio >=100, stopping at the pad metal; the alumina barrier at each pore bottom is thinned by a voltage ramp-down and removed by a short wet or atomic-layer etch. An ALD Al2O3 liner seals the anion-contaminated pore walls, then TiN / ZrO2-Al2O3-ZrO2 (or the B2-02/B2-03 dielectric) / TiN cup capacitors are ALD-coated inside the pores. The rigid alumina honeycomb stays in place as the mechanical support lattice, so there is no pillar leaning and no SiN support-lattice masks. The bit is stored and sensed exactly as in a 1T1C cell (Si BCAT or IGZO 4F2 VCT access device).
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 storage-capacitor charge wall (HAR etch, leaning/collapse) and A1 #4 capital/masks of the capacitor module; A2 PFAS/fluorocarbon chokepoint (the C4F6/C4F8 HAR SiO2 etch).
ideas.step_change_claim: Capacitor 2.5-3 um tall (pore AR ~100-115) with no plasma HAR etch: Cs 7.4-8.9 fF at a 4F2 40 nm-pitch cell (+37-64% vs 1-beta's 5.4 fF) at ~1-beta-parity density with periphery under cell; capacitor-hole module goes from ~3 masks + fluorocarbon HAR etch + SiN lattice to 1 imprint + wet anodization (~8 Wh/wafer).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-01: 4F2 at F=20 nm -> 40 nm square pitch (the bottom of AAO's demonstrated 40-500 nm interval). Pore widened to 26 nm (porosity 0.33); after a 3 nm TiN liner and a ~5 nm dielectric the mid-plane diameter is ~15 nm. C = 3.9*eps0*pi*d*h/EOT with EOT 0.55 nm: h=2.5 um -> 7.40 fF; 3.0 um -> 8.88 fF (1-beta pillar 21 nm x 1.3 um -> 5.38 fF, matches A1). Density 4F2 F=20 nm: 0.319 Gb/mm2 at array eff 0.51 (0.71x 1-beta), 0.438 Gb/mm2 with periphery-under-cell eff 0.70 (0.98x). Anodization: 0.19 g Al/wafer, 2,011 C, 8.4 Wh at 15 V vs ~1,300 kWh/wafer fab total (A2). Scaling check: UMD AAO capacitance rises ~linearly with pore depth (11 -> 26 uF/cm2 from 1 to 2 um).

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known: ALD MIM nanocapacitors in AAO (UMD/Rubloff 2009) and imprint-ordered AAO (Masuda) are known for energy storage and templates; using registered AAO as the DRAM cell-capacitor mold with the alumina walls as the permanent support lattice is a NEW combination (no DRAM use found).
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Pitch: ideally ordered AAO is reported at 40-500 nm intervals; today's 1-beta/1c honeycomb is 32-35 nm, at or beyond the edge. (2) Removing the alumina barrier at the bottom of 20-26 nm pores without attacking the landing pad, with imprint-to-pad overlay of ~3-4 nm. (3) Electrolyte anions and charge in AAO walls (and pore branching at Al grain boundaries) add leakage, traps and defects.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Target 4F2 at F=20 nm (40 nm pitch), where AAO is demonstrated, and get density from 4F2 plus periphery-under-cell rather than pitch; Kondo-style mold-interval reduction for later shrinks; Cs scales with height, so 3-4 um pores buy margin. (2) Anodize onto a thin valve-metal stop layer (Ti/Nb) that converts to a removable oxide; voltage ramp-down barrier thinning; self-aligned landing pads (B2-14) relax overlay. (3) ALD Al2O3 passivation liner (UMD needed it for leakage) plus <=450 C anneal; large-grain or Al-Cu films; residual defects absorbed by repair/ECC (B2-15).
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 18 months, ~$350k of the $1M: sputter Al on 100-150 mm wafers with TiN pad arrays at 40-60 nm pitch (e-beam-written pads), imprint-pretexture and anodize; SEM-map ordering and pore-bottom opening defects over mm2 areas (~$120k of nanofab time). ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN in the pores; measure C, J at 0.5 V (target <=1e-7 A/cm2), breakdown and per-capacitor C spread with small addressable test arrays (~$130k). Integrate 64x64 1T1C cells using a university IGZO TFT layer under the AAO (~$100k).
ideas.resource_angle: Removes the fluorocarbon (PFAS-class, high-GWP) HAR etch and the SiN lattice from the capacitor module; Al is abundant (0.19 g/wafer); room-temperature wet electrochemistry at ~8 Wh/wafer; fewer plasma-etch hours (less helium-cooled chuck time); no EUV.
ideas.us_buildable: UMD FabLab, College Park MD (Rubloff AAO lineage); Cornell CNF (Ithaca NY); Georgia Tech IEN (Atlanta); NIST CNST (Gaithersburg MD); a MEMS-style 200 mm line such as SkyWater (Bloomington MN) for a later pilot.
ideas.triage_reason: Anodization physics (interval ~2.5 nm/V, barrier ~1.2 nm/V) gives a 40 nm interval at ~16 V; imprint pretexturing gives ideal ordering, and ALD MIM in AAO pores is demonstrated with capacitance linear in depth (Banerjee 2009). Today's 32-35 nm honeycomb is beyond reported AAO intervals, so the card correctly targets 4F2 at 40 nm pitch. Pore-bottom barrier removal over a pad and anion-contaminated walls are integration, not physics.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: imprint-guided pores at 40 nm pitch cannot reach >=2 um depth with <1e-4 branched or missing pores, or pore-bottom opening attacks the landing pad.
ideas.claim_short: Self-ordered anodic-alumina capacitor mold: Cs 7.4-8.9 fF from 2.5-3 um pores, no fluorocarbon HAR etch

ideas.name: Ru-free rutile: SnO2-templated TiO2 short-stub capacitor
ideas.one_liner: Get k 60-100 rutile TiO2 at 250-340 C by growing it on abundant, conductive, rutile-structured doped SnO2 instead of scarce Ru/RuO2, and spend the gain on a much shorter capacitor.
ideas.mechanism: Cap the TiN bottom electrode with 3-5 nm of ALD Ta-, Nb- or F-doped SnO2 (conductive, rutile/cassiterite structure, a=4.74 A vs rutile TiO2 a=4.59 A). ALD TiO2 (optionally lightly Al-doped to suppress leakage) nucleates epitaxially in the rutile phase on the SnO2 grains at 250-340 C, giving k ~60-100 without the >800 C anneal or the Ru/RuO2 template used in earlier rutile work. A doped-SnO2 top electrode makes the stack symmetric and keeps the high-work-function contact. At 7 nm physical thickness the EOT is 0.34-0.40 nm. The capacitor is used either to shorten the 1-beta pillar from 1.3 um to 0.8-0.95 um, or as a 0.30-0.35 um stub holding ~2 fF for short-bitline, 4F2 or 3D-tier cells.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor wall (k>60 needed) and A1 #2 (a capacitor that fits a 3D tier); A2 warning that Ru electrodes fleet-wide need 26-176% of world Ru and HZO needs 14-41% of separated Hf.
ideas.step_change_claim: 1.4-1.6x more capacitance per area than ZrO2-based stacks (EOT 0.40/0.34 vs 0.55 nm): equal Cs from a capacitor 27-38% shorter (AR ~39-45 instead of 62), or 2 fF from a 0.30-0.35 um stub; zero Ru and zero Hf.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-02: k=68 (Gordon 2010) at 7 nm -> EOT 0.401 nm -> h(5.4 fF, d=21 nm)=0.95 um, h(2.0 fF)=0.35 um; k=80 -> 0.81/0.30 um; k=100 -> 0.65/0.24 um. Leakage budget: sidewall area of the 0.95 um stub = 6.3e-10 cm2, so J=1e-7 A/cm2 -> 0.063 fA/cell vs 13 fA (64 ms), 0.84 fA (1 s), 0.084 fA (10 s); J=1e-5 -> 6.3 fA still meets 64 ms. So a Si-BCAT DRAM tolerates J up to ~1e-5 at the storage bias, while a 10 s oxide-channel cell needs <=~1e-7 at ~0.5 V. Sn use: 0.44 g/wafer at 15% ALD utilization -> ~10 t/yr fleet = ~0.003% of world tin [world tin UNVERIFIED-PK].

ideas.novelty: KNOWN (Harvard/Gordon 2010 rutile TiO2 on SnO2; KIST Ta:SnO2 template; patent filings on doped-SnO2 seeds) | TWIST: aimed at the Ru-free short-stub regime for short-bitline, 4F2 and 3D-tier cells, and at oxide-channel cells where dielectric leakage, not the transistor, sets retention.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Leakage: rutile TiO2's ~3.0-3.2 eV gap and the small conduction-band offset to SnO2 may push J above 1e-7 A/cm2 at 0.5-0.8 V. (2) Template continuity: a crystalline, continuous 3-5 nm SnO2 film on HAR sidewalls; grain boundaries nucleate anatase (k<40) and leak. (3) Hydrogen/forming-gas anneals reduce SnO2 and TiO2 (oxygen vacancies -> conduction).
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Al-doped TiO2 or a 0.3-0.5 nm Al2O3 interlayer (trading some k), high-work-function top electrode, and operation at half-VDD plate bias; per the arithmetic, a 64 ms-1 s product already tolerates 1e-6-1e-5 A/cm2. (2) Ta:SnO2 is reported to template rutile and survive 400 C; O3-based conversion steps from the patent literature; thicker SnO2 only at the bottom electrode. (3) Use the oxide-channel BEOL flow, which already avoids forming gas (imec H+O anneal).
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 12-18 months, ~$250k: planar and 1-2 um deep-trench MIM test structures on Si; ALD doped SnO2 + rutile TiO2 at 250-340 C; XRD/TEM phase, C-V, J-V at 25-125 C, TDDB. Pass bar: EOT <=0.40 nm at J <=1e-7 A/cm2 at 0.5 V and 85 C. Then pair with a university IGZO access TFT for a 1T1C retention test (~$80k extra).
ideas.resource_angle: Avoids Ru (fleet-scale demand 26-176% of world supply) and Hf (14-41%); Sn and Ti are abundant (~10 t/yr Sn fleet-wide). Dopant choice matters: Ta is a conflict mineral and Nb is ~90% Brazilian [UNVERIFIED-PK], so F- or W-doped SnO2 is preferred. Shorter capacitors also cut HAR etch time.
ideas.us_buildable: Harvard CNS (Cambridge MA, Gordon ALD lineage); Purdue Birck (IN); NC State (Raleigh); Penn State MRI (State College PA).
ideas.triage_reason: Rutile templating on SnO2 at <=340 C is published (Gordon 2010; KIST). The risk is leakage of a 3.0-3.2 eV-gap dielectric at EOT <=0.4 nm, but a 64 ms Si cell tolerates ~1e-5 A/cm2 (B2 arithmetic), so a physics window exists for conventional DRAM; oxide-channel cells need ~1e-7 A/cm2.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: EOT <=0.40 nm cannot be reached at <=1e-6 A/cm2, 0.5 V, 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Ru-free rutile TiO2 on doped SnO2: EOT 0.34-0.40 nm, capacitor 27-38% shorter, zero Ru/Hf

ideas.name: Hf-free MPB zirconia with work-function-biased operating point
ideas.one_liner: Reach k ~55-60 without hafnium by tuning Zr-only ZrO2 stacks to the tetragonal/polar-orthorhombic boundary and using asymmetric electrodes to park the DRAM operating window on the steep part of the permittivity curve.
ideas.mechanism: Today's DRAM uses Al-doped ZrO2 (k ~40, EOT ~0.6-0.7 nm). The highest reported hafnia-zirconia k values (56-64) sit at the morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) between ferroelectric-orthorhombic and tetragonal phases, using HZO superlattices that contain Hf. Here the stack is Zr-only ZrO2 (5.5-6 nm) whose phase balance is set by dopant (Al, Si, Y), thickness and electrode strain. An antiferroelectric-like ZrO2 has its highest small-signal permittivity near its field-induced transition; a built-in bias from work-function-asymmetric electrodes (TiN bottom, doped-SnO2 or MoO2 top) shifts that peak into the 0-0.5 V storage window. The capacitor is otherwise a standard pillar or stub.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor wall; A2 Hf warning (HZO fleet-wide = 14-41% of separated world Hf; Hf price ~$5k -> ~$13k/kg in 2025-26).
ideas.step_change_claim: EOT 0.55 -> ~0.41 nm (k 40 -> 56): the same 5.4 fF from a 0.97 um pillar instead of 1.29 um (AR 62 -> 46), or +34% Cs at the same height, Hf-free. A modest step on its own; it compounds with B2-01 (taller AAO cups) or B2-08 (shorter bitlines).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-03: k=40 at 5.6 nm -> EOT 0.546 nm -> h=1.29 um (AR 62); k=56 at 5.9 nm -> 0.411 nm -> 0.97 um (AR 46); k=62 -> 0.371 nm -> 0.88 um (AR 42), all at d=21 nm and 5.4 fF. Zr demand is unchanged from today (~19 t/yr fleet, <0.01% of Zr, A2).

evidence.shows: Al-doped ZrO2 is the commercial DRAM dielectric, EOT limited to ~6-7 A; MPB between ferroelectric-orthorhombic and tetragonal phases is the high-k route (via search snippet)

evidence.title: KAIST record 10203/303175: ZrO2/HZO bilayer MPB capacitor

evidence.title: POSTECH: Accurate evaluation of high-k HZO/ZrO2 films by morphotropic phase boundary

evidence.title: J. Mater. Chem. C 2026 (D5TC02886H): MPB capacitance evaluation
evidence.shows: capacitance at MPB compositions is overestimated by standard measurements; k-optimal composition differs between low- and high-voltage regimes (via search snippet)

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known: MPB HZO superlattices (KAIST, POSTECH, SNU) and antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitors are known; Hf-free MPB plus electrode-asymmetry biasing of the operating point is the twist (not found in the snippets).
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) A 2026 J. Mater. Chem. C paper reports MPB capacitance is overestimated by standard measurement; the small-signal k at 0-0.5 V may stay ~40. (2) Operating near a field-induced phase transition brings hysteresis loss, fatigue and slow charge relaxation (looks like leakage or charge loss). (3) Below ~6 nm the tetragonal phase dominates and leakage rises at EOT ~0.4 nm.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Measure only with ns-pulsed small-signal C at DRAM bias; if the gain vanishes, fold the work into B2-02 TiO2/ZrO2 laminates. (2) Bias the window into the reversible paraelectric shoulder, not across the transition; 1e15-cycle pulsed endurance testing decides. (3) Laminate with thin Al2O3 for leakage and use oxidation-tolerant oxide top electrodes.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 12 months, ~$150k: planar MIM matrix (3 dopants x 3 thicknesses x 3 electrode pairs) by university ALD; ns-pulsed C-V at 0.3-0.6 V, J-V at 85 C, 1e12-1e15 cycle endurance at 50 ns pulses. Pass bar: small-signal k >=52 at 0.5 V, J <=1e-7 A/cm2, no fatigue to 1e13.
ideas.resource_angle: Hf-free (Hf is separation-limited and under Chinese export control); Zr is plentiful. It shortens HAR etch only modestly.
ideas.us_buildable: UT Dallas (Richardson TX, ALD/high-k groups); NC State; Penn State MRI; Georgia Tech IEN.
ideas.triage_reason: k enhancement near the tetragonal/orthorhombic boundary is reported for HZO, but a 2026 J. Mater. Chem. C paper says standard measurements overestimate it; whether a genuine small-signal k >=55 survives at ns, at DRAM bias and without hysteresis loss is contested. The step is modest (1.34x) even if true.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when ns-pulsed small-signal C at 0-0.5 V shows k >=55 in Zr-only films with <=1e-7 A/cm2 and no charge relaxation over 64 ms.
ideas.claim_short: Hf-free MPB zirconia, asymmetric electrodes: k 40 -> ~56; pillar 1.29 -> 0.97 um

ideas.name: Capacitor-first inverted flow with perovskite super-k
ideas.one_liner: Build and crystallize a perovskite (Ba,Sr)TiO3 capacitor array at 650-750 C before any transistor exists, then grow low-temperature oxide access transistors on top and bond the periphery last, so the thermal-budget conflict that killed perovskite DRAM disappears.
ideas.mechanism: On a bare carrier or Si wafer, deposit a conductive-oxide bottom electrode (LaNiO3, Nb:SrTiO3 or doped SnO2), sputter/ALD 10-12 nm (Ba,Sr)TiO3 or SrTiO3 into short pillars or cups, and RTA at 650-750 C to crystallize (k 100-250); add the top electrode and planarize. Then build vertical IGZO/ZTO access transistors directly on the capacitor top contacts at <=400 C (the OCTRAM-style transistor-over-capacitor arrangement), and finally hybrid-bond the logic periphery wafer on top. Because the capacitor comes first, no transistor, metal or gate stack ever sees the perovskite anneal. The bit is a normal 1T1C charge sensed through a short bitline.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 (k>=100 needed for a <=300-500 nm capacitor), A1 #2 (a stub that fits a tier), A1 #4 (HAR etch).
ideas.step_change_claim: 3-4x shorter capacitor at equal charge: k 150 (EOT 0.26 nm) gives 4.6 fF from a 0.5 um stub (vs 5.4 fF from 1.3 um today), AR ~23 instead of 60-75; a 0.3 um stub gives 1.8-3.8 fF, enough for 64-128-cell bitlines.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-04 (d=22 nm pillar at a 40 nm-pitch 4F2 lattice): k=100/10 nm (EOT 0.39) -> 1.84 fF at 0.3 um, 3.06 fF at 0.5 um; k=150/10 nm (EOT 0.26) -> 2.75/4.59 fF; k=250/12 nm (EOT 0.19) -> 3.82/6.37 fF. Leakage: SrTiO3 at EOT 0.42 nm showed ~1e-6 A/cm2 (A1 cross-ref); over a 0.5 um stub's 3.5e-10 cm2 that is ~0.35 fA, acceptable for 64 ms-1 s retention but not for 10 s.

ideas.novelty: NEW combination: process-order inversion (capacitor-first, high-temperature perovskite) enabled only by oxide-channel transistors plus bonded periphery. Perovskite (BST) DRAM capacitors were pursued in the 1990s-2000s and abandoned over integration and electrodes [UNVERIFIED-PK]. That OCTRAM places the IGZO transistor above the capacitor is from prior knowledge [UNVERIFIED-PK].
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Thin-film perovskite k collapses (dead layers, grain size vs a 22 nm pillar) and leaks (~3.2 eV gap). (2) Electrodes: oxidation-resistant contacts are traditionally Pt/Ru/SrRuO3 (scarce); LaNiO3 needs La (China-processed rare earth). (3) Conformal perovskite deposition in 3D (Ba/Sr ALD precursors are poor) and interdiffusion during the anneal.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Target the short-stub regime (AR <=25), where sputter or ALD/sputter hybrids suffice, and accept 64 ms-1 s retention products; Al2O3 interlayers for leakage. (2) LaNiO3 from Mountain Pass (U.S.) lanthanum or doped-SnO2 electrodes; no Ru. (3) Crystallize planar or shallow-cup capacitors first; the transistor-on-top flow needs no conformal 60:1 coating.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 18 months, ~$300k: planar and 300-500 nm cup BST/STO capacitors on LaNiO3 at 650-750 C; then a <=350 C IGZO TFT on top; measure C, J, k vs thickness and 1T1C retention at 85 C. Pass bar: >=2 fF from a <=0.5 um cup at J <=1e-6 A/cm2 and 0.5 V.
ideas.resource_angle: Ba, Sr and Ti are abundant; Ru-free if LaNiO3 or SnO2 electrodes work; far less HAR etch. Negative: La or Nb electrodes add rare-earth or Brazil-concentrated inputs.
ideas.us_buildable: Penn State MRI (perovskite thin films); Cornell PARADIM (Ithaca NY); Purdue Birck for the IGZO top layer.
ideas.triage_reason: BST/STO crystallizes at 650-750 C, which an oxide-channel transistor built afterwards never sees, so reversing process order is legitimate. Thin-film dead layers cut k at <=10 nm and the ~3.2 eV gap leaks, but k >=100 at EOT ~0.3-0.4 nm in ALD STO is reported [UNVERIFIED-PK], so the window is open at short-stub aspect ratios (AR <=25).
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: a crystallized BST/STO stub at AR <=25 cannot deliver k >=100 with <=1e-6 A/cm2 at 0.5 V and 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Capacitor-first perovskite (BST, k~150): 3-4x shorter capacitor, oxide transistors built on top

ideas.name: Solid-state proton double-layer nano-capacitor [SPECULATIVE]
ideas.one_liner: Store the DRAM charge in an electric double layer across a few-nm solid proton electrolyte (phosphosilicate glass), which holds 2-16x more charge per area than ZrO2, so a 0.1-0.4 um stub replaces a 1.3 um pillar.
ideas.mechanism: Replace the high-k film with a 3-5 nm PECVD phosphosilicate-glass (PSG) proton conductor between ion-blocking TiN or W electrodes, optionally with a 1-2 nm pseudocapacitive WO3 or MnO2 skin. Applying the bit voltage (<=~1 V) moves protons a fraction of a nm to form double layers at both interfaces: an all-solid-state nano-supercapacitor with ~10-20 uF/cm2 (EDL) or ~100 uF/cm2 (pseudocapacitive) vs 6.3 uF/cm2 for EOT 0.55 nm. The access transistor and sensing are unchanged. MIT showed nanosecond proton shuttling through PSG at room temperature under ~1 V/nm fields.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor wall (charge per footprint), A1 #2 (capacitor in a tier).
ideas.step_change_claim: 5.4 fF from a 0.41 um stub (EDL, 20 uF/cm2) or 0.08 um (pseudocapacitive, 100 uF/cm2) at 21 nm diameter, vs 1.3 um today: 3-16x shorter, with all-abundant P/Si/O/H/W.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-05: ZrO2-class EOT 0.55 nm = 6.28 uF/cm2. Height for 5.4 fF at d=21 nm: 10 uF/cm2 -> 0.82 um, 20 -> 0.41 um, 100 -> 0.08 um. Speed: R_ion = t/(sigma*A) for a 5 nm film over 2.7e-10 cm2: sigma 1e-3 S/cm -> RC 10 ns, 1e-4 -> 100 ns, 1e-5 -> 1 us. DRAM-class write needs effective sigma >=1e-3 S/cm, plausible only in the high-field regime MIT reported. Retention: electronic leakage at 1e-6 A/cm2 over 2.7e-10 cm2 = 0.27 fA (meets 64 ms and 1 s).

evidence.title: Onen et al., Nanosecond protonic programmable resistors for analog deep learning (Science 377, 539, 2022)
evidence.shows: controlled proton shuttling/intercalation in nanoseconds at room temperature through phosphosilicate glass (PSG) electrolyte under ~1 V/nm; WO3/PSG/Pd stack (via search snippet)

evidence.title: IBM/MIT: CMOS-compatible protonic programmable resistor based on PSG electrolyte
evidence.shows: back-end-CMOS-compatible PSG proton electrolyte (Nano Letters 2021) (via search snippet)

ideas.novelty: [SPECULATIVE] NEW combination: protonic PSG electrolytes are known as analog synapses (MIT/IBM); using a solid electrolyte double layer as the DRAM storage capacitor was not found.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) At storage-level fields (~0.1 V/nm) proton mobility may be orders of magnitude below the 1 V/nm regime, giving RC far above 100 ns. (2) Self-discharge: Faradaic side reactions, redox shuttles and electronic leakage over hours, strongly temperature-activated. (3) Mobile hydrogen next to an IGZO channel causes H-doping and PBTI drift.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Write with a short high-field overdrive pulse, store at low field; screen nanoconfined conductors (PSG, hydrated ZrO2) for room-temperature sigma >=1e-3 S/cm. (2) Ion-blocking electrodes, a narrow voltage window (<=0.8 V) and retention-aware refresh; a 1 s target (16x DRAM) is enough to be useful. (3) Al2O3/SiN hydrogen barriers between capacitor and channel, or pair with a Si or 2D access device that tolerates H.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 12 months, ~$200k: planar and 1 um trench TiN/PSG/TiN MIM structures; impedance from 1 kHz to 100 MHz, 10-100 ns pulsed charge/discharge, leakage and self-discharge at 25-85 C, 1e12-cycle endurance. Kill test: if the 100 ns charging fraction is <50% at 0.8 V, stop.
ideas.resource_angle: P, Si, O, H, W and Mn are abundant; PECVD at BEOL temperatures; no Hf, Ru or Zr; shorter HAR etch.
ideas.us_buildable: MIT.nano (Cambridge MA; del Alamo/Yildiz/Li lineage); Sandia CINT (Albuquerque NM) user facility.
ideas.triage_reason: B1 rejected a protonic stub as thermodynamically contradictory; that argument applies to storing information in ion POSITION, not to a double-layer capacitor, whose state is electronic charge on blocking electrodes and whose retention is set by electronic/faradaic leakage, not ion mobility. So the EDL version (10-20 uF/cm2 vs 6.3 uF/cm2 for EOT 0.55 nm) is physically allowed. Unproven: a 3-5 nm solid electrolyte with sigma_H+ >=1e-3 S/cm at storage fields (RC <=10 ns per the card) and EDL capacitance that does not disperse away at >=100 MHz; mobile H next to IGZO.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a TiN/PSG/TiN MIM shows >=50% of its low-frequency EDL charge in a 10 ns pulse at 0.8 V, and <=1e-6 A/cm2 leakage at 85 C.
ideas.claim_short: Solid proton double-layer nano-capacitor: 2-3x (EDL) charge/area; 0.41 um stub
dead_subclaims: 100 uF/cm2 pseudocapacitive WO3/MnO2 skin: faradaic insertion at 1e12-1e15 cycles is battery-class chemistry (B5 R11)

ideas.name: Gallium-free, indium-lean oxide channels (ZTO / SnO2 / ITZO) for gain cells and VCT
ideas.one_liner: Make the oxide-channel DRAM wave independent of China-controlled gallium (and mostly of indium) by switching IGZO/IGO channels to zinc-tin oxide or In-lean tin oxides; Ga-free ZTO 2T0C already holds data >1500 s.
ideas.mechanism: Deposit amorphous Zn-Sn-O (ZTO), SnO2, or In-lean In-Sn-Zn-O / In-W-O channels by ALD (or PVD for planar) at <=350 C, with the gate insulator and channel grown in one ALD chamber without a vacuum break (UMich) and Al2O3/SiO2 passivation (Hf-free, unlike the HfO2 used for the SJTU record). Cells are the same 2T0C/3T0C gain cells or 4F2 VCT access transistors now built with IGZO. Zn and Sn suppress oxygen-vacancy carriers less strongly than Ga, so thin (3-5 nm) channels, Al or Si doping, and O3 anneals set the threshold voltage. The bit is stored on the read transistor's gate (gain cell) or on a capacitor (VCT).
ideas.which_bottleneck: A2 chokepoint: Ga is ~98% Chinese and the U.S. export-ban suspension ends 2026-11-27; In refining is concentrated. Keeps A1 #3 (oxide leakage -> long retention).
ideas.step_change_claim: 100% Ga-free (and In-free for ZTO) oxide DRAM supply chain at >=1500 s demonstrated retention (~23,000x a 64 ms refresh interval), with 2-6 ns single-bit read on a 64-cell read bitline.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-07: read bitline C = 0.1 fF/cell + 5 fF (A3); 64 cells = 11.4 fF. 100 mV develops in t = C*dV/I: 0.2 uA (ZTO at ~1/3 of IGZO drive) -> 5.7 ns; 0.6 uA -> 1.9 ns; 3-bit (8x) -> 15-46 ns. ideas.name: In-tier complementary-oxide sense amplifiers (no-bond short bitlines)
ideas.one_liner: Use the new p-type oxides (TeSeOx, SnO) with n-IGZO/ZTO to build local sense amps as a BEOL tier right next to each memory tier group, so every 64-cell bitline segment gets its own amplifier without wafer bonding.
ideas.mechanism: Build complementary oxide TFT latch sense amplifiers (n-IGZO/ZTO + p-TeSeOx, mobility ~15 cm2/Vs, on/off 1e6-1e7) in a dedicated BEOL tier above or below the memory tier(s), connected by short vias to 64-cell local bitline segments. Short bitlines (Cbl ~8 fF instead of ~35 fF) cut the needed storage capacitance to ~1.2 fF and allow VARY ~0.4 V; the local SA restores the cell and drives a global bitline to the Si periphery. In 3D stacks one SA tier serves N memory tiers, so bitline capacitance no longer grows with tier count. Offset-cancelled (auto-zero) SA topology absorbs oxide Vt mismatch.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #10 voltage floor, A1 #1 (Cs requirement), A1 #7 periphery area (~49% of the die), A1 #2 (bitline routing in 3D).
ideas.step_change_claim: ~27x lower bitline CV2/2 energy per sense (17.5 -> 0.64 fJ) and ~4.5x lower Cs requirement (5.4 -> ~1.2 fF), monolithically, without a second bonded wafer.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-08: 512-cell BL 35 fF at 1.0 V -> 17.5 fJ; 64-cell 8 fF at 0.4 V -> 0.64 fJ (27x). Area: a 64-cell segment at 4F2 F=20 nm covers 0.102 um2, so an open-BL SA serving two segments gets 0.205 um2 per tier; stacked over 4/8/16 tiers it gets 0.82/1.64/3.28 um2. Offset: oxide sigma(Vt) ~40 mV [ASSUMPTION] -> 6-sigma pair offset ~339 mV, above the 215 mV fresh 64-cell signal (A1), so offset cancellation is mandatory.

ideas.name: Ge-free, NAND-line 3D oxide gain cell (oxide/nitride mold + channel replacement)
ideas.one_liner: Build 3D DRAM the way 3D NAND is built (deposited SiO2/SiN mold, one hole etch, replacement), with capacitorless oxide gain cells, instead of epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattices that need germanium and single-crystal tiers.
ideas.mechanism: Deposit 16-64 SiO2/SiN pairs by PECVD (standard NAND tools). One HAR hole/slit etch exposes all tiers; SiN is removed with hot phosphoric acid and replaced in every tier by ALD IGZO/ZTO horizontal channels (Kioxia's 3D OCTRAM SiN->InGaZnO replacement) plus recessed W/Mo gate and storage-node fills. Vertical wordline pillars gate the write transistors through all tiers (IMECAS dual-gate vertical-WL 2T0C); each storage node is a metal island that gates the tier's read transistor, so no lateral capacitor is needed. 2-3 bits/cell with write-verify multiplies the tier count.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 (no manufacturable 3D DRAM cell), A1 #4 (bits by deposition, not lithography); A2: Si/SiGe superlattices fleet-wide need 6-38% of refined world Ge; reuses NAND capital and cleanroom.
ideas.step_change_claim: 1.1-3.4x 1-beta density at F=40 nm with 16 tiers (1-3 bits), 6.8x at 32 tiers x 3 bits, with no EUV, no Ge and no epitaxy; runs on 3D-NAND tool sets.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-09 (vertical 2T0C 10F2, eff 0.508, A3 convention): F=40, 1 b x 16 tiers -> 0.51 Gb/mm2 (1.1x); 3 b x 16 -> 1.52 (3.4x); 3 b x 32 -> 3.05 (6.8x); F=30, 2 b x 32 -> 3.61 (8.1x). Ge avoided: 9-53 t/yr fleet-wide (A2). Tier break-even per A1 is ~26 for a capacitor-bearing 1T1C; deleting the capacitor drops it to the 10F2 footprint.

ideas.name: Fluorine-free carbon mold for capacitor holes and sacrificial 3D tiers
ideas.one_liner: Make the HAR molds out of amorphous carbon, etched with O2/COS or H2/N2 plasma and removed by oxygen, so the largest-volume HAR etches in DRAM need no fluorocarbon (PFAS-class) gas at all.
ideas.mechanism: Replace the SiO2 capacitor mold with a 1.3-2.5 um PECVD amorphous-carbon film (the 3D-NAND hardmask material) capped by a thin SiN or Al2O3 support lattice. Holes are etched anisotropically in O2/COS or H2/N2 plasma (sulfur or nitrogen sidewall passivation, no fluorine). ALD electrode and dielectric (or oxide channel) fill the holes; the carbon is then burned out by O2 or removed by H2 plasma, leaving free-standing, lattice-supported structures. In 3D stacks, carbon replaces SiN as the sacrificial tier: a low-pressure thermal O2 burn is reaction-limited, so the lateral recess is uniform from top to bottom of the stack, and the product is CO2.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A2 PFAS/fluorochemical chokepoint (EU restriction ~2028+, 3M exit); A1 #1/#2 HAR etch and 3D lateral-recess uniformity.
ideas.step_change_claim: Eliminates fluorocarbon gas from the capacitor/channel-hole modules (~5.6e13 HAR holes per wafer at 1-beta) and makes 3D lateral recess a thermal, reaction-limited step; the mold leaves ~0.6 g CO2/wafer instead of PFAS-class by-products.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-10: one capacitor hole per 1,070 nm2 cell -> 9.35e8 holes/mm2 -> 5.6e13 per wafer. A 1.3 um a-C mold (1.8 g/cm3) is 0.17 g C per wafer -> 0.61 g CO2 on burn-out. The low-GWP replacements under study (C2F4O: -24-29% GWP; HFO-1234ze) are still fluorinated, so this is a 100% rather than a 25% cut for these steps.

(2) Oxidation-tolerant conductive-oxide electrodes (doped SnO2, B2-02) or H2-plasma carbon removal; nucleation layers. (3) Count it as removing the largest fluorocarbon consumers first; remote-plasma O2/H2 chamber cleans where possible.

ideas.resource_angle: PFAS-free and far lower GWP for these steps; carbon comes from hydrocarbons; exits the exposure to fluorochemical supply and regulation.
ideas.us_buildable: Cornell CNF (Ithaca NY, which also hosts a 2026 PFAS-etch project); Penn Singh Center; UT Austin Texas Materials Institute.
ideas.triage_reason: a-C hardmasks etched with O2/COS are standard; using carbon as the sacrificial mold raises mechanics (bow at AR 50-100) and electrode oxidation during the O2 strip, both engineering.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: carbon molds at AR >=40 with 20 nm holes show >2 nm wiggle/bow that boron doping and support decks cannot fix.
ideas.claim_short: Fluorine-free amorphous-carbon HAR molds; PFAS-class gases out of capacitor/channel modules

ideas.name: DSA honeycomb: block-copolymer self-assembly for the capacitor/channel hole lattice
ideas.one_liner: The hexagonal lattice that cylinder-forming block copolymers assemble into is the DRAM capacitor honeycomb; register it with a relaxed ArF guide and let thermodynamics do the EUV's job.
ideas.mechanism: Coat PS-b-PMMA (or a high-chi BCP for <30 nm) whose cylinder lattice period L0 (~28-40 nm) matches the 1-beta (35 nm) or 1c (32 nm) capacitor honeycomb. A single-exposure ArF immersion guide pattern (or chemical pre-pattern) at 2-3x the pitch registers the lattice and DSA multiplies density 3-4x, rectifying CD and placement noise. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O into PMMA) hardens the pattern into an AlOx mask for transfer into the mold (SiO2 or the carbon mold of B2-10). For 4F2 square lattices, chemo-epitaxy with a square guide is used.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 litho-bound scaling and EUV dependence; A2 EUV single-supplier chokepoint.
ideas.step_change_claim: Replaces 1-2 EUV or SAQP layers in the array: $165-330 per wafer (3.8-7.7% of a $4.3k 1c wafer) before netting DSA cost; the hole lattice comes from polymer physics rather than wavelength.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-11..14: removing 1/2/3 EUV layers saves $165/330/495 per wafer = 3.8/7.7/11.5% of a 1c wafer. Lattice match: imec used a 37 nm-pitch BCP for contact-hole multiplication (BACUS 2014); 1-beta honeycomb 35 nm, 1c 32 nm (A1). A guide at ~70-105 nm pitch is single-exposure ArF immersion territory (no multipatterning).

ideas.us_buildable: Argonne CNM (Lemont IL, SIS); Brookhaven CFN (Upton NY); UChicago PME; MIT.

ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: DSA hole lattices stay above ~1e-4 per-site defects or >2 nm placement error after anneal optimization.

ideas.name: NIL-only periodic cell wafer (bonded periphery makes every layer imprintable)
ideas.one_liner: Once the periphery lives on a separate bonded logic wafer, the cell wafer contains only perfectly periodic arrays, which is exactly what nanoimprint does best, so pattern every critical cell layer by imprint and drop EUV and SAQP from it.
ideas.mechanism: A master template (e-beam- or DSA-written) is replicated into working templates; jet-and-flash imprint defines each field's hole or line lattice with no projection optics. Because the cell wafer of a bonded 4F2 VCT or vertical gain-cell array needs only 2-3 overlay-critical layers (channel holes, wordline, contact) and later layers self-align, NIL's overlay and pattern-variety weaknesses matter less. 3D templates can define line + contact in a single imprint (dual-damascene style). Defects are absorbed by redundancy and ECC (B2-15).
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 (EUV, capex, depreciation ~55% of wafer cost), A2 EUV single supplier (~65 tools/yr, ~10 GWh/yr each).
ideas.step_change_claim: No EUV and no SAQP spacer loops on array layers: 2-3 imprint layers replace ~4-6 EUV/SAQP-patterned layers [ESTIMATE], worth ~$330-500/wafer at EUV rates; litho tool capex per wafer start plausibly several-fold lower [UNVERIFIED-PK on tool price].
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-11..14: 2-3 EUV layers at $165 = $330-495/wafer (7.7-11.5% of a 1c wafer). Overlay budget for DRAM critical layers = 15-20% of half pitch (NIL review): at F=20 nm that is 3-4 nm, about 1.4x looser than at 14 nm (2.1-2.8 nm).

ideas.name: Maskless interference lithography for an all-periodic cell wafer
ideas.one_liner: Pattern the periphery-free cell wafer with two-beam 193 nm immersion interference fringes (no mask, no projection lens): ~35 nm half-pitch lines, crossed for hole lattices, one spacer step to F~17 nm 4F2.
ideas.mechanism: Two (or four) coherent 193 nm beams interfere in water immersion to write a fringe pattern at half-pitch ~34.5-36 nm; two crossed exposures give post or hole lattices at ~70 nm pitch, and one SADP halves that to ~35 nm. Scanning-beam interference lithography (Doppler writing) phase-locks the fringe to wafer marks for overlay and covers 300 mm continuously. Array edges and the few non-periodic features are cut by a coarse KrF/i-line trim exposure whose overlay is not critical. Possible only because bonded periphery has removed all random logic from the cell wafer.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 (litho capex, EUV), A2 EUV single-supplier chokepoint and capital per bit.

ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Layer-to-layer overlay: fringe-phase placement to the previous layer at <=3 nm over 300 mm with wafer distortion. (2) Dose and fringe-contrast uniformity, defect-free fields, and stitching (SBIL was built for continuous gratings). (3) Only infinite periodic patterns: array termination, wordline/bitline ends and periphery contacts need another litho.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Only the first critical layer needs IL if later layers are self-aligned (spacers, ASD B2-14); SBIL-style interferometric phase locking. (2) Scan-and-stitch with phase metrology; B2-15 defect tolerance. (3) Coarse trim exposures on cheap KrF/i-line tools; bond pads at relaxed pitch.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 18 months, ~$300k: build a tabletop 193 nm (or 213/266 nm dry) two-beam interference exposure with a phase-locked stage; expose 100 mm wafers; measure CD uniformity, LER, defects/cm2 and two-layer overlay; transfer one lattice into a 2T0C channel-hole mold.
ideas.resource_angle: No EUV, no photomasks (mask sets cost $M), far lower litho capex and power; DUV lasers instead of EUV sources.
ideas.us_buildable: MIT (Space Nanotechnology Lab, SBIL heritage); UNM Center for High Technology Materials (Albuquerque, interferometric lithography heritage); RIT (Rochester NY).

ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: fringe-to-layer overlay cannot be held <=3 nm (3 sigma) across a distorted 300 mm wafer.

ideas.name: ASD self-aligned landing pads and top contacts
ideas.one_liner: Grow the storage-node landing pads and vertical-channel top contacts bottom-up by area-selective deposition so they self-align to the plugs below and a dedicated critical lithography layer disappears.
ideas.mechanism: After the contact plugs are exposed in dielectric, Mo (or W) is deposited by area-selective ALD/CVD that nucleates only on metal or semiconductor surfaces, with small-molecule or SAM inhibitors on the dielectric and periodic atomic-layer-etch 'defect clean' cycles to remove stray nuclei. The pad grows a controlled height and mushroom width, self-aligned to its plug, so the landing-pad litho/etch step (patterned with EUV or multipatterning at leading nodes [UNVERIFIED-PK]) is not needed. The same approach caps vertical oxide channels in 4F2 VCT and gain-cell arrays.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 masks/EUV; A1 #2 (self-aligned contacts in 3D); A2 tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%).
ideas.step_change_claim: -1 to -2 critical litho layers (~$165-330/wafer if EUV-patterned; 3.8-7.7% of a 1c wafer) and fewer fluorocarbon etches; Mo replaces WF6-based W.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-11..14 for the layer cost. Selectivity requirement: with ~1.7e10 pads per 16 Gb die and repair able to handle ~1e4-1e5 random fails (more with B2-15), the stray-nucleus bridging probability must be <=1e-6-1e-5 per pad gap. Mushroom growth = pad thickness, so a 15 nm gap allows <=7 nm of over-growth per side.

ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Selectivity loss: stray nuclei bridge 10-15 nm gaps (killer defects). (2) Lateral overgrowth equal to film thickness. (3) Variable nucleation delay on tiny plugs leads to non-uniform pads.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Deposition/etch supercycles and inhibitor chemistries; B2-15 tolerance. (2) Thin pads plus a self-aligned dielectric cap; 4F2 layouts with larger gaps. (3) Pre-clean and seed treatments; Mo chemistries with short nucleation delay.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 12 months, ~$150k: Mo ASD on W/TiN plugs in SiO2 at 40-80 nm pitch; electrical comb/serpentine tests over ~1e8 gaps to measure bridging rate; TEM of pad shape. Pass bar: bridging <=1e-6 per gap.
ideas.resource_angle: Fewer masks and EUV exposures; Mo (U.S. mines) instead of W (China ~80%, APT +350% in 2026); fewer fluorocarbon etch steps.
ideas.us_buildable: NC State (Raleigh, ASD groups); CU Boulder (ALE); Stanford (ASD inhibitors).
ideas.triage_reason: ASD is nucleation-delay chemistry already used for self-aligned vias; stray nuclei and lateral overgrowth are process windows, not physics limits.

ideas.claim_short: Area-selective-deposition self-aligned landing pads: -1 to -2 critical litho layers

ideas.name: Defect-budget co-design: 100x pattern-defect tolerance to unlock cheap patterning
ideas.one_liner: Specify the array to survive a 1e-4 random cell-defect fraction (vs ~1e-6 assumed today) with t=2 BCH ECC in the logic periphery and a tiny remap table, so NIL, DSA, interference litho, AAO and panel processes become usable.
ideas.mechanism: Every 128-bit word carries 16 BCH (t=2) check bits instead of 8 SECDED bits, decoded in fast logic-process periphery (bonded or under-array). A small CAM remaps the few residual failing words found at test; mat-level sparing (NAND bad-block style) handles clustered pattern defects (line opens, shorts). Retention-weak cells are remapped too. This turns patterning defectivity from a yield killer into a few percent of area overhead.
ideas.which_bottleneck: Enabling layer for A1 #4 (cheap patterning) and A1 #2 (3D tier yield ~0.998/tier needed); A2 capital per bit.
ideas.step_change_claim: Random-defect tolerance x100 (p 1e-6 -> 1e-4) for +6.25% extra check bits and ~65 remap words per 16 Gb die.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-15 (16 Gb die, 1.34e8 words of 128 bits): p=1e-4 -> 1.72M defective cells; SECDED (136,128) failing words = C(136,2) p^2 x words ~12,336; BCH t=2 (144,128) failing words = C(144,3) p^3 x words ~65. At p=1e-5: 123 vs 0.1. The ECC must also cover soft errors and retention tails, so the defect budget is set at ~1e-4, not higher.

ideas.novelty: KNOWN principle (heavy ECC in NAND; on-die ECC in DDR5/HBM) | TWIST: making pattern-defectivity tolerance an explicit design input so DRAM-class arrays can use NAND-like cheap patterning.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) ECC decode latency and energy at DRAM speed, and read-modify-write for partial writes. (2) Soft errors, retention tails and row hammer share the same ECC budget. (3) Real pattern defects cluster (lines, blocks), which random-error ECC does not fix.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Logic-process periphery decodes t=2 BCH in ~1-3 ns [ESTIMATE]; 64 B access granularity. (2) Scrubbing; oxide gain cells have long retention and may be hammer-resistant (untested). (3) Mat and column sparing plus remap for clusters.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 9 months, ~$100k: FPGA emulation with fault injection driven by measured defect maps from the B2-11/12/13 demos; a t=2 BCH decoder on a 28 nm MPW shuttle (~$60k) to measure latency and energy.
ideas.resource_angle: Lets cheaper, lower-energy, EUV-free patterning be used; lowers scrap.
ideas.us_buildable: Anywhere with FPGA tools; MPW via a U.S.-accessible TSMC/GF shuttle broker.
ideas.triage_reason: Coding theory, with the arithmetic checked in the card. Clustered defects need sparing in addition, which is standard practice.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: real pattern defects cluster beyond what mat/column sparing absorbs.
ideas.claim_short: Design for a 1e-4 random-defect fraction with t=2 BCH: 100x pattern-defect tolerance for +6.25% bits

ideas.name: Main memory inside the logic die's own metal stack (monolithic BEOL oxide gain cells)
ideas.one_liner: Build 8-16 tiers of 3-bit oxide gain cells directly in the upper BEOL of the GPU/CPU die at <=400 C, putting tens of GB of DRAM-class memory microns from the compute with no DRAM wafer, no TSVs and no HBM stack.
ideas.mechanism: After the logic metal stack is complete (TSMC has already embedded an oxide-semiconductor-selector memory fully in BEOL above advanced logic), deposit 8-16 tiers of vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C cells with 3 bits/cell write-verify, local complementary-oxide sensing (B2-08) and short vias down to SRAM-buffered memory controllers. Oxide cells retain >200 s at 95 C, so they tolerate sitting on hot logic. On backside-power logic, the frontside BEOL is less congested. Capacity is the target, not cache: an 800 mm2 die area carries 76-152 GB.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #5 interface energy (HBM ~3-4 pJ/bit), A1 #6 HBM TSV tax (~3x wafer per bit), A1 #3 (hot retention); A2 prime wafers and HPQ crucibles.
ideas.step_change_claim: 76-152 GB over an 800 mm2 die (3 b x 8-16 tiers at F=40 nm, no EUV); interface energy 3.5 -> ~0.2 pJ/bit, saving 211-422 W per accelerator at 8-16 TB/s; zero extra wafers; added cost ~$0.87/GB at $500 per tier per wafer and 80% yield.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-16: vertical 2T0C 10F2, F=40 nm, eff 0.508: 3 b x 8 tiers -> 0.76 Gb/mm2 -> 76 GB per 800 mm2; x16 tiers -> 1.52 Gb/mm2 -> 152 GB. Added $/GB = tiers x $500 / (Gb/mm2 x 60,334 mm2 / 8 x 0.8) = $0.87/GB regardless of tier count (vs DDR5 $1.48 cost, HBM3E $6.08). Power: (3.5-0.2) pJ/bit x 8 TB/s x 8 = 211 W; 16 TB/s -> 422 W.

ideas.one_liner: Build the memory cell stack in a fab that has only low-temperature BEOL tools, on a reusable glass carrier, then bond it to a periphery wafer from any U.S. 28-65 nm foundry: DRAM capacity without a DRAM fab.
ideas.mechanism: Oxide gain-cell or oxide 1T1C stacks (8-32 tiers) are deposited and patterned on a 300 mm CTE-matched glass carrier with a laser-release layer, using only PVD/ALD/PECVD, dry etch, ArF/NIL, CMP, cleans and a hybrid bonder: no >450 C furnaces, implanters, epitaxy or EUV. The finished stack is hybrid-bonded face-down to a periphery wafer (sense amps, decoders, I/O) from a trailing-node foundry at 1-2 um pitch, which A3's model says is enough for litho-light oxide pitches. The glass is laser-debonded through its transparent back and reused.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A2 #1 binding constraint (capital x cleanroom time per bit); A2 HPQ/prime-wafer chokepoint; A1 #7 periphery area.
ideas.step_change_claim: Cell-side capex ~$44-68k per wafer-start-per-month vs $145-170k for a DRAM greenfield (2.5-3.3x lower) [ASSUMPTION: BEOL-only tool set = 30-40%]; prime-Si demand of dual-wafer (periphery-under-cell) DRAM -45-49% by reusing the cell carrier 10-50x.

Capex: $145-170k/wpm (A1) x 0.30-0.40 = $44-68k/wpm. Bond count: one bond per 128-256-cell segment at oxide pitches -> 1-1.6 um bond pitch (A3 model section 7).

ideas.name: Trailing-node fab reuse: CMOS-under-array deep-tier MLC oxide memory at F=65 nm
ideas.one_liner: Turn a depreciated 65-90 nm logic fab into a DRAM-class memory fab: periphery CMOS in the existing flow, then 16-24 tiers of 3-4-bit oxide gain cells stacked over it, patterned with the fab's existing dry-ArF/KrF tools.
ideas.mechanism: Run the fab's 65 nm CMOS flow to build sense amps, decoders and write-verify DACs, then stack 16-24 tiers of vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C cells over them (CMOS-under-array, as in 3D NAND CuA), with one hole etch per tier group at F=65 nm, ALD channels and recessed gates. Each cell stores 3-4 bits by write-verify; long oxide retention gives the level stability that MLC needs. No bonding, no immersion, no EUV.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A2 capital and cleanroom time (reuse existing U.S. fabs), A1 #4 (litho-bound scaling), A3 white space 1 (MLC x tiers).
ideas.step_change_claim: 1.8-2.7x 1-beta density and 1.7-3.5x 1-beta bits per wafer-dollar (before yield) at F=65 nm, in existing depreciated fabs with no new litho tools.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-18: vertical 10F2 at F=65 nm needs bits x tiers = 37 (eff 0.508) or 27 (CuA eff 0.70) to match 1-beta. 3 b x 16 tiers, eff 0.70 -> 0.80 Gb/mm2 (1.78x). Wafer = $1,300 (depreciated line, ram-venture) + tiers x $80-162: 3 b x 16 -> 2.62x (at $80/tier) or 1.73x (at $162/tier, A2 convention) bits/$; 4 b x 16 -> 3.49x/2.31x; 3 b x 24 -> 3.15x/1.95x. ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Start at Gen 2.5 or 300x300 mm; tile-local patterning means overlay only matters within a tile. (2) Seams become scribe lanes; B2-15 defect tolerance. (3) In-tile sensing and serialization so tiles need only ~10-40 um-pitch bumps.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 18 months, ~$300k (simulation + coupons): 8-tier oxide stack on 100-150 mm glass, imprint at 100-200 nm pitch, one hole etch, ALD channel; tier uniformity and cell function; a panel-scale cost and defect model.
ideas.resource_angle: No CZ silicon or HPQ crucibles; reuses display-class tools. Caveat: glass making is energy-intensive and the U.S. has no TFT panel fab (ram-venture).
ideas.us_buildable: Coupons only: university fabs (Cornell CNF, GT IEN); U.S. specialty-glass suppliers; no U.S. panel line exists.
ideas.triage_reason: No new physics: density comes from tiers (3 b x 64 at F=100 nm = 0.96 Gb/mm2). Glass compaction, panel-scale HAR etch and imprint seams are tool-scale engineering, and overlay matters only inside a tile.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: glass compaction/distortion at 400 C exceeds the intra-tile overlay budget (~20 nm at F=100 nm) after 64 tiers.
ideas.claim_short: Panel-level (Gen 3.5) 64-128-tier oxide memory imprinted at F~100 nm: ~45 TB per panel

ideas.name: Self-assembled tier stack: parallel block-copolymer lamellae + sequential infiltration synthesis [SPECULATIVE]
ideas.one_liner: Spin one micron-thick block-copolymer film that self-organizes into 25-80 substrate-parallel layers, convert alternate layers to AlOx by vapor infiltration, and use it as the 3D mold: tens of tiers from one coat instead of tens of PECVD depositions.
ideas.mechanism: A lamella-forming BCP (L0 25-40 nm) with preferential wetting on both interfaces orders parallel to the substrate after annealing, giving 25-80 alternating layers in a 1-2 um film. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) converts the PMMA layers into AlOx sheets; the PS layers remain as sacrificial carbon tiers (removed later by oxidation, as in B2-10). A single hole etch then opens all tiers; lateral recess and ALD oxide-channel/gate fills proceed as in B2-09. Tier thickness is set by polymer molecular weight rather than deposition time.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 (tier cost and count for 3D DRAM), A2 capital and cleanroom time (PECVD stack deposition is a long, tool-heavy step).
ideas.step_change_claim: 25-80 tiers per coat vs one PECVD pair per tier: tier-formation tool time ~10-50x lower [ESTIMATE]; no SiN/SiGe stack.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-20: periods = film thickness / L0: L0 25 nm -> 40 (1 um) or 80 (2 um) tiers; L0 40 nm -> 25-50 tiers. Tier-thickness tolerance ~+/-1 nm (4% of 25 nm) is needed; L0 scales ~N^(2/3), so molecular-weight dispersity sets the floor [UNVERIFIED-PK].

ideas.novelty: [SPECULATIVE] NEW combination: parallel lamellae and SIS are each known (SIS developed at Argonne [UNVERIFIED-PK]); using them as a self-assembled 3D-DRAM tier mold was not found. No search was spent on this card.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Long-range parallel order with +/-1 nm layer uniformity through a micron-thick film; dislocations and undulations. (2) Mechanics and thermal stability: AlOx sheets need supports; polymers survive only ~250-300 C before conversion. (3) SIS penetration depth in thick films.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Coat 8-16 periods at a time and repeat; high-chi, low-dispersity BCPs; crosslinkable blocks. (2) Convert fully to inorganic (AlOx/carbon) before any ALD; add support pillars in the first hole etch. (3) Long-exposure or pressure-pulsed SIS; thinner sub-stacks.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 12 months, ~$150k: 10-20-period parallel lamellae on 100 mm wafers; SIS conversion; cross-section TEM layer-thickness statistics; one hole etch and ALD IGZO into the recesses; a single-tier transistor test.
ideas.resource_angle: Replaces dozens of SiH4/TEOS/NH3 PECVD steps with one coat plus vapor infiltration; lower energy and tool time; commodity polymers (solvent use instead of dry deposition).
ideas.us_buildable: Argonne CNM (Lemont IL); UChicago PME; Brookhaven CFN (Upton NY).
ideas.triage_reason: Parallel lamellae and sequential infiltration are both real, and equilibrium defect energies are high, but long-range defect-free order through 25-80 periods (~1 um) with +/-1 nm layer uniformity has never been shown; thick lamellar films develop undulations, terraces and dislocations whose annealing kinetics may be too slow for any process time.
ideas.revival_condition: Promote to ALIVE when a >=25-period lamellar film converted by SIS shows <=1 nm thickness sigma and <1 dislocation per 10 um2.
ideas.claim_short: Self-assembled tier stack: one BCP coat -> 25-80 parallel lamellae converted by SIS

ideas.name: MSB-DRAM: hierarchical 64-cell bitlines with sense amps bonded under the array
ideas.one_liner: Cut every bitline into 64-cell segments, gang 8 of them through in-array pass switches onto one hybrid bond, and put the sense amp on a logic wafer underneath: the storage capacitor shrinks from 1.3 um to ~0.34-0.44 um and bond pitch relaxes to ~0.74-1.05 um.
ideas.mechanism: Keep a conventional 1T1C cell (Si BCAT, or an oxide 4F2 VCT) but break each bitline into 64-cell local segments. Eight local segments in a column each connect through one pass transistor (built in the cell process) to a short global bitline that drops through a single Cu-SiCN hybrid bond to a sense amplifier on a separately made logic periphery wafer bonded face-to-face (Samsung's periphery-under-cell scheme, but at sense-amp granularity). Only the segment holding the activated wordline is switched on, so the sense amp sees ~9 fF instead of ~35 fF. By the A1 sense criterion the capacitor needed falls from 5.4 fF to ~1.4-1.8 fF, a 335-445 nm stub instead of a 1.3 um pillar; alternatively keep the tall capacitor and drop the array voltage toward ~0.4 V. Sense amps, sub-array decoders and I/O leave the cell wafer, lifting array efficiency from ~0.51 to ~0.70.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor charge wall, #10 array voltage floor and #7 periphery overhead; and the bond-pitch gap inside A1 white space 1 (one bond per 64-128-cell bitline needs 0.26-0.37 um pitch, beyond production hybrid bonding).
ideas.step_change_claim: Capacitor aspect ratio 62 -> 16-21 (3-4x shorter, no AR-60 capacitor etch); bitline energy per sensed bit 3.9x lower at today's VARY, or ~22x lower at VARY ~0.4 V with the tall capacitor; 1.37x density from array efficiency; bond pitch 0.74-1.05 um instead of 0.26-0.37 um. Cost per bit ~1.1-1.3x 1-beta in 2D (an energy and capacitor win, not a cost win, until stacked).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: c_cell = (35-8)/(512-64) = 0.060 fF from A1's bitline table. Local BL = 64 x 0.060 + 0.1 = 3.96 fF; global = 8 segments x 1.72 um x 0.15 fF/um + 8 x 0.05 fF off-switch junctions + 1.0 fF bond pad + 1.5 fF SA input = 4.96 fF; Cbl_eff = 8.9 fF (pessimistic 11.8 fF). A1 criterion (VARY 1.06 V, 50 mV after 15% droop) gives Cs >= 0.156*Cbl = 1.39 fF (1.84 fF) -> pillar 335 nm (443 nm) at 21 nm diameter, EOT 0.55 nm (check: the same formula returns 5.45 fF at 35 fF, matching A1's 5.4). Energy Cbl*V^2/2: 35 fF -> 19.7 fJ; 8.9 fF -> 5.0 fJ; keeping 5.4 fF, VARY_min = 0.38 V -> 0.9 fJ at 0.45 V. Bond area 8 x 64 x 1,070 nm2 = 0.548 um2 -> 0.74 um pitch (16:1 -> 1.05 um); SA budget 1.1-2.2 um2, ample for a ~10-transistor offset-cancelled latch at 28-40 nm. Density 0.447 x 0.70/0.51 = 0.614 Gb/mm2. Cost $3,650 cell + $1,800-3,000 periphery + $200 bond = $5,650-6,850 for 1.37x bits -> 1.08-1.31x 1-beta $/bit. (models/B3_3dprocess_estimates.py section B3-01)

(2) 0.74-1.05 um hybrid-bond pitch with >=99.999% per-bond yield across a 16Gb die (~30M bonds at 8:1). (3) Pass-switch leakage and Vt mismatch add sense-amp offset.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Drop to 4:1 mux as bond pitch improves, or switch to B3-22 (lithographic vias, no bond pad, saves ~2 fF). (2) Duplicate bond pads per global bitline at 1.05 um pitch plus column repair. (3) Offset-cancelling (auto-zero) sense amps are cheap on a logic wafer and fit in 1.1-2.2 um2.

ideas.triage_reason: Pure charge-sharing arithmetic (Cs >= 0.156 Cbl with Cbl_eff ~9 fF -> 1.4-1.8 fF) on known parts: hierarchical bitlines and ~1 um hybrid bonding.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: Cbl_eff with mux and bond pad >12 fF, or per-bond yield <99.999% at ~1 um pitch.
ideas.claim_short: 64-cell local bitlines muxed 8:1 to bonded sense amps: capacitor 3-4x shorter; bond pitch 0.74-1.05 um

ideas.name: Carrier-is-memory: the mandatory carrier wafer of backside-power logic becomes a DRAM wafer
ideas.one_liner: Every backside-power (PowerVia / A16-class) logic wafer is already bonded face-down to a blank silicon carrier; hybrid-bond a DRAM wafer there instead and each accelerator gets ~45-53 GB at ~0.3 pJ/bit with no TSVs, no interposer and no added footprint.
ideas.mechanism: In backside power delivery the finished front-side BEOL is flipped and bonded to a carrier wafer, the original substrate is ground away and power is wired in from the back, so the front-side signal wiring ends up facing the carrier. Replace that blank carrier with a full DRAM wafer (1-beta-class 1T1C or an oxide-cell wafer) whose die map matches the logic reticle, and make the bond a Cu-SiCN hybrid bond at 1-2 um pitch instead of a plain dielectric fusion bond. The memory die keeps its sense amps and bank logic but drops pads, PHYs and TSVs; commands, data and memory power cross the bond. The memory wafer stays thick and becomes the heat-spreading side of the stack (pair with B3-03). For a wafer-scale engine, the same move puts a whole 300 mm DRAM wafer (~3.9 TB) under the compute wafer.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #5 interface energy (HBM 3-4 pJ/bit, 224-448 W per accelerator), A1 #6 HBM TSV/stacking tax, and A2 white space 1 (bits per cleanroom-hour: an ordinary DRAM wafer instead of HBM's ~3x wafer per bit).
ideas.step_change_claim: Memory interface energy ~12x lower (3.5 -> ~0.28 pJ/bit), saving ~200-410 W per accelerator at 8-16 TB/s; 45-53 GB per 800 mm2 logic die with zero added footprint and no HBM stacking; ~$1.7-2.3/GB of added memory at DRAM-wafer cost.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Capacity: 800 mm2 x 0.447 Gb/mm2 = 44.7 GB; with pads/PHY removed (array eff 0.51 -> 0.60) 0.526 Gb/mm2 -> 52.6 GB. Interface: 12 fF (pad + 50 um wire) x (0.75 V)^2 x 0.5 activity = 0.003 pJ/bit + 0.5 mm on-die move 0.10 + streaming activation 0.18 (A1) = 0.28 pJ/bit; at 16 TB/s HBM 448 W -> 36 W (8 TB/s: 224 -> 18 W). Bond ceiling: 1 um pitch = 1e6 bonds/mm2; 2% used as 2 Gb/s lanes = ~4,000 TB/s, so the array and power bind first. Cost: ($3,800 - $120 carrier) / 60 dies / logic yield 0.5-0.7 = $88-123 per good accelerator = $1.7-2.3/GB. Refresh in the heat path: 421 Gb x 0.75 mW/Gb = 0.32 W at 64 ms, 1.26 W at 16 ms (105 C), negligible against ~1 kW. Wafer-scale: 70,686 mm2 x 0.85 x 0.526 Gb/mm2 = 3.9 TB. (models/B3_3dprocess_estimates.py section B3-02)

(2) The hybrid bond must survive BSPDN backside processing (grind to ~1 um, nano-TSVs, backside metal) and the wafer distortion that bonding/thinning already causes for backside lithography. (3) The memory sits in the heat path at 85-105 C.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Design the memory die for >=99% die yield with 10-20% spare rows/banks and ECC, and ship capacity-binned parts (e.g., a 48 GB bin from a 53 GB design); DRAM wafers already yield ~90%. (2) The carrier bond already has to survive backside processing; Cu-SiCN bonds anneal at <=350-400 C, within DRAM BEOL limits. (3) Refresh at 105 C costs only ~1.3 W per layer; B3-03 cooling or oxide cells remove even that.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: Real BSPDN wafers need a foundry partner after the seed. For ~$350k: die-to-wafer hybrid bond a DRAM test die (or a university oxide-cell array) face-to-face onto a 28 nm MPW logic die at 2-6 um pitch, thin the logic side below 5 um to emulate BSPDN, and measure bond yield, data-path pJ/bit and retention vs temperature; plus a ~$50k thermo-mechanical simulation of a 1 kW BSPDN stack with a memory carrier.

ideas.triage_reason: Backside power delivery requires a front-side carrier bond, and the logic's signal BEOL faces that carrier, so a hybrid-bonded memory wafer there is electrically natural. The memory sits in the heat path at 85-105 C, costing ~1.3 W per 52 GB of extra refresh (card): no physics barrier. Wafer-to-wafer compound yield is the engineering risk.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: hybrid bonds degrade through BSPDN thinning and nano-TSV steps, or memory-layer distortion breaks backside litho overlay.
ideas.claim_short: The BSPDN carrier slot becomes a hybrid-bonded DRAM wafer: 45-53 GB per accelerator at ~0.28 pJ/bit

ideas.name: Coolant-backed memory wafer: microchannels in the memory layer of a memory-on-logic stack
ideas.one_liner: Etch microfluidic channels into the back of the memory wafer that sits on top of the logic, so the DRAM rides ~10-30 K above coolant instead of at GPU junction temperature, and ordinary Si DRAM can refresh every ~0.5-1 s instead of every 16-64 ms.
ideas.mechanism: In a face-to-face memory-on-logic stack (B3-02, or any bonded DRAM-over-logic), etch 100-200 um deep microchannels into the back of the thick memory wafer, away from its devices, and run warm water through them. The memory devices then sit only ~50 um of silicon plus their own BEOL from the coolant, while the logic's heat crosses the memory on its way out. With in-silicon microchannels of the kind Microsoft and Corintis demonstrated in 2025, the memory layer runs ~9-28 K above coolant instead of at the 70-105 C of a cold-plate GPU junction. DRAM retention roughly doubles for every 10 C drop, so a Si 1T1C array at ~45 C holds a 64 ms tail cell for ~1 s.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 leakage tail -> refresh energy and refresh busy-time; the thermal blocker in A1 #5 (retention collapses on hot logic); A2's use-phase energy (~16x fab energy per GB).
ideas.step_change_claim: Refresh energy and refresh busy-time 8-16x lower for ordinary Si DRAM (64 ms -> 0.5-1 s; 7.6% -> 0.5-0.9% of time), and standard DRAM becomes viable directly on 1 kW logic without switching to oxide cells.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: q = 1,000 W / 8 cm2 = 1.25 MW/m2. Memory rise = q/h + q*(50 um / 148 W/mK) + q*(5 um / 3 W/mK): h = 1e5 W/m2K -> 12.5 + 0.4 + 2.1 = 15 K (h 5e4 -> 27.5 K; 2e5 -> 8.8 K); logic ~4 K hotter. Coolant at 30 C -> memory ~39-58 C. Retention gain 2^((85-T)/10): 45 C -> 16x (1,024 ms refresh, busy 7.6% -> 0.47%); 55 C -> 8x; 65 C -> 4x. Hot spots at 3-5x mean flux push local memory 40-60 K above coolant: handle with per-bank temperature-compensated refresh. (models/B3_3dprocess_estimates.py section B3-03)

absorbed_cards.name: Thermal arbitrage: keep the bits away from the GPU's heat
absorbed_cards.one_liner: DRAM's worst enemy is the accelerator's heat. A 35 C liquid-cooled memory sled buys 4-30x retention, which pays for refresh cuts, multi-level rows or shorter capacitors.
absorbed_cards.mechanism: HBM sits millimetres from a ~1 kW GPU at 85-95 C (32 ms refresh above 85 C), and server DIMMs run 50-85 C. In a disaggregated design, capacity DRAM (KV pools, cold weights, CXL expanders) moves onto separately liquid-cooled sleds at 30-40 C, linked by optics (B4-14) or CXL. Refresh is set from on-die temperature and canary readings (B4-02), not the 85 C worst case. The cool margin can be spent three ways: (a) 4-30x longer refresh intervals; (b) multi-level rows (B4-05), whose droop budget is a third of single-level; (c) next-generation dies designed to a 'cool spec' with ~30% shorter capacitors.
absorbed_cards.which_bottleneck: A1 #3 refresh and #1 capacitor (via retention margin); trades against #5 interface energy
absorbed_cards.step_change_claim: Retention x3.7-18 from 85 C to 35 C (Arrhenius, Ea 0.25-0.55 eV; x32 by the 2x/10 C rule), so refresh energy and busy time fall 4-18x; or Cs 5.4 -> ~3.8 fF (the sense-limited floor), a ~30% shorter pillar.
absorbed_cards.first_principles_estimate: 85 -> 35 C: the rule of thumb gives 2^(50/10) = 32x. Arrhenius exp[(Ea/k)(1/308 - 1/358)] gives 3.7x for Ea 0.25 eV (GIDL/trap-assisted tail) and 18x for 0.55 eV (SRH junction generation); 95 -> 35 C gives 4.6-29x. Capacitor: with tail leakage /16, a 3.8-4.0 fF cell droops only ~13-14 mV in 64 ms, so Cs is bounded by the no-droop sense floor of 3.7 fF on a 512-cell bitline. Cost: link energy ~2-3 pJ/b (optical) vs ~3.5 pJ/b for HBM, plus ~100-300 ns latency, so this suits capacity tiers only. (card13)

absorbed_cards.novelty: NEW combination. Pooled and disaggregated memory (Celestial AI, CXL) is pursued for capacity and stranding, and cryogenic DRAM uses temperature at 77 K (A3 killed it on fridge energy). I found no design that uses ordinary 30-40 C liquid cooling specifically to harvest retention, then redesigns refresh and cells around a cool spec.
absorbed_cards.show_stoppers: (1) Tail leakage may be dominated by weakly activated mechanisms (GIDL, trap-assisted tunnelling, Ea ~0.2-0.3 eV), capping the gain at ~3-5x. (2) Distance costs latency (~100-300 ns) and link energy, so it cannot serve bandwidth-critical HBM duty. (3) Sled power density and coolant temperature limits.
absorbed_cards.revival_or_workaround: (1) Measure retention-vs-temperature tails at 25-95 C on modern dies; it is cheap and decisive. If Ea is low, combine with B4-02 so the ECC, not the tail, sets the interval. (2) Restrict to capacity tiers (KV pools, B4-09's full-KV tier). (3) 25-30 C coolant is standard in direct liquid cooling.
absorbed_cards.million_dollar_demo: ~$0.18M. A thermal-chamber retention study (FPGA tester, 25-95 C, 100 chips) fits Arrhenius curves to the 1e-9-1e-5 tails (~$80k). Then a liquid-cooled CXL memory sled (commercial CXL expander plus cold plate) shows 4-16x longer refresh intervals with B4-02 scrubbing (~$100k).
absorbed_cards.resource_angle: Use-phase energy; less refresh-driven bandwidth loss; a path to shorter capacitors (less HAR etch, less ALD precursor).
absorbed_cards.us_buildable: Anywhere; CXL expanders and cold plates are commercial.

ideas.triage_reason: Merged with B4-13. The Arrhenius retention gain from 85 to 35 C is x3.7 (Ea 0.25 eV) to x18 (0.55 eV) (C0-14), worth 8-16x less refresh or a ~30% shorter capacitor. The open physics question is the activation energy of today's tail cells: GIDL/trap-assisted tails (Ea ~0.2-0.3 eV) would cap the gain at ~3-5x.

ideas.name: Coaxial 4F2 2T0C: the storage node is the core gate of a read-channel shell
ideas.one_liner: Put a whole capacitor-less gain cell in one vertical pillar: a metal storage-node core wrapped by an oxide read channel, with the write transistor stacked on top, so a 2T0C fits 4F2 per tier and matches 1-beta density at 4 bit-tiers with single-exposure ArF litho.
ideas.mechanism: Each cell is one pillar on a 2F x 2F grid. The core is a metal storage node (~20 nm diameter, ~150 nm tall) wrapped by a gate dielectric and an ALD IGZO/IGO shell; the shell is the read transistor's channel and the core is its gate (an inverted channel-all-around device), contacted by a source plane at the bottom and a read-bitline ring at the top. Above the core sits the write transistor: a short vertical oxide channel gated by a write-wordline ring, linking the write bitline at the pillar top to the core. Four line levels (source rows, read-bitline columns, write-wordline rows, write-bitline columns) each run at 2F pitch at different heights, so the 2T0C occupies 4F2 per tier. Tiers stack monolithically at <=400 C over CMOS-under-array.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 (no capacitor at all), #2 (3D per-tier footprint, the reason 2T0C needs b x N >= 15 at F = 40 nm in A3), #3 (oxide leakage gives long retention), #8 (non-destructive read).
ideas.step_change_claim: Per-tier density 2.5-3.4x better than A3's 10F2 vertical 2T0C: 1-beta parity at bits x tiers = 4.1 at F = 40 nm (no EUV, no multipatterning) vs 14; 2 bits x 8 tiers at F = 40 nm = 3.9x 1-beta density and ~2.5x bits per wafer-dollar before yield.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Density = 1e12/(4F2) x 0.70 (CMOS-under-array): F = 40 nm -> 0.109 Gb/mm2 per tier-bit (A3 10F2 at eff 0.508: 0.032). Break-even b x N: 4.1 (F = 40), 2.3 (F = 30), 1.0 (F = 20); at equal efficiency 0.508: 5.6 vs 14.1. Cost (base wafer 0.55 x $3,800 at F = 40 plus $475/tier): 2b x 8 = 1.75 Gb/mm2 at $5,890/wafer -> 2.53x bits/$; F = 30, 2b x 4 -> 2.9x. Storage node C = 3.9 eps0 x pi x 20 nm x 150 nm / 2 nm EOT = 0.163 fF (~1,000 e/V). Retention at 200 mV droop: 3,250 s at 10 zA total leakage, 325 s at 100 zA, 33 s at 1 aA; 2-bit (50 mV) 4x shorter. Read: shell perimeter ~94 nm x 10 uA/um = 0.94 uA -> 100 mV on 9 fF in 0.95 ns. Write-wordline kickback 75-211 mV for 0.005-0.015 fF coupling. (models/B3_3dprocess_estimates.py section B3-04)

ideas.novelty: TWIST on IMECAS: IME CAS has shown a 4F2 dual-gate 2T0C with vertically stacked transistors. The twist is the coaxial inversion (the storage node as the core gate of a read shell, so the read transistor is the storage capacitor and its full channel area sets C_SN), four orthogonal line levels, and monolithic multi-tier stacking over CMOS. Not found in this form.
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Kickback and coupling on a 0.16 fF node: the falling write wordline couples 75-211 mV. (2) ~1,000 electrons per volt makes 2+ bits/cell sensitive to single trap events and PBTI drift. (3) Four line levels at 2F pitch need ~F/4 (10 nm at F = 40) vertical overlay between levels.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Drop the write bitline before the write wordline falls, use a negative wordline hold, or subtract the kick with a dummy reference cell; a 300 nm core doubles C_SN to 0.33 fF. (2) Ship 1 bit/cell first (still 2x 1-beta at 8 tiers) and add write-verify 2-bit once drift data exist; use H-resilient In-poor IGZO. (3) Pillar-first, self-aligned flow where line levels are set by deposition thickness and only the hole lattice is lithographic.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: ~$350k at a university nanofab: single-tier coax cells at F = 60-100 nm (e-beam or i-line plus spacer), ALD IGZO; measure read current, C_SN, retention at 25-125 C, kickback, 2-bit write-verify. Then a 2-tier stack and a 64 x 64 array with an FPGA tester (~$150k). Decisive metric: >=100 s at 85 C with <=50 mV kick after compensation.
ideas.resource_angle: No capacitor module, no EUV at F = 40 nm, no single-crystal Si; In/Ga in milligrams per wafer; Ga-free channels (ITZO/ZTO, B2-07) remove the Chinese gallium licence risk.
ideas.us_buildable: Purdue Birck, Georgia Tech IEN, Notre Dame NDnano, Penn Singh Center; 300 mm path at NY CREATES Albany.
ideas.triage_reason: A gate-all-around oxide read FET around a metal core is ordinary device physics, and IMECAS has a 4F2 dual-gate 2T0C. The 0.16 fF node (~1,000 e-/V) makes write-wordline kickback (75-211 mV) and single-trap noise real, but circuit-addressable.
ideas.revival_condition: Alive. Kill test: >=100 s retention at 85 C with <=50 mV residual kick cannot be reached in a single-tier coax cell.
ideas.claim_short: Coaxial 4F2 2T0C (storage node = core gate of the read channel): 1b parity at 4 bit-tiers with single-exposure ArF

ideas.name: Mirror-VCT: 4F2 oxide cells above and below one shared bitline plane (2F2 effective)
ideas.one_liner: Samsung's 4F2 VCT already flips the cell wafer to bond its periphery; build a second, mirror-image VCT layer on the exposed backside of the same bitline plane and every bitline serves two cells, doubling density with DUV-only patterning.
ideas.mechanism: Build a 4F2 vertical-channel 1T1C array (deposited IGZO/IGO pillars, ring wordlines) over a buried bitline plane, with capacitors on top, as in Samsung's VCT. Bond that face to the periphery wafer (the periphery-under-cell flow already flips the cell wafer), remove the handle down to the back of the bitline plane, and build a mirror-image 4F2 VCT array plus capacitors from the backside at <=400 C. Each bitline now connects cells above and below it, so one bitline layer, one set of bitline contacts and one periphery wafer serve two cell layers: 2F2 effective per bit. The backside module is all-deposited (ALD oxide channel, ALD ZrO2 MIM), so it never exceeds BEOL temperatures.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 litho-bound scaling and capital (density from structure, not wavelength), A1 #2 (a two-layer 3D step without a new cell type).
ideas.step_change_claim: 2x density over single-sided 4F2: 0.88 Gb/mm2 (1.96x 1-beta) at F = 20 nm with DUV multipatterning only, or 1.62 Gb/mm2 (3.6x) at F = 14.7 nm; ~1.4-1.5x bits/$ vs single-sided VCT.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Per side 1e12/(4F2) x 0.70: F = 20 -> 0.44 Gb/mm2; F = 14.7 -> 0.81. Mirrored: 0.88 / 1.62 Gb/mm2. If the backside VCT + capacitor module adds 35-45% to the cell+periphery stack cost, bits/$ = 2/(1.35-1.45) = 1.38-1.48x vs single-sided. Backside overlay must be <= ~F/4 = 5 nm (F = 20) after bond-induced distortion. Bitline load per unit length doubles, so halve the segment length or combine with B3-01. (models/B3_3dprocess_estimates.py section B3-05)

ideas.name: Ge-free dopant-contrast superlattice (Si / Si:B) for 3D silicon DRAM
ideas.one_liner: Replace the strained Si/SiGe superlattice of 3D Si DRAM with lattice-near-matched Si / heavily-boron-doped Si layers removed by dopant-selective etching, cutting misfit strain ~5-16x and Ge use 5-16x (or to zero).
ideas.mechanism: 3D silicon DRAM (Samsung VS-DRAM, SK hynix, imec) starts from an epitaxial Si/Si0.8Ge0.2 superlattice whose SiGe layers are later etched out to free horizontal Si channels; imec's 120-bilayer stacks still show dislocations because the 0.84% mismatch accumulates strain, and A2 puts fleet-scale Ge demand at 6-38% of refined supply. Instead grow intrinsic Si alternating with heavily boron-doped Si (1-3e20 cm-3, optionally carbon co-doped, or with ~1-4% Ge to null the small lattice contraction) by the same low-temperature RPCVD. Remove the sacrificial layers through the slit with dopant-selective chemistry: an HF/HNO3/CH3COOH etch that attacks heavily doped Si far faster than intrinsic Si, or selective electrochemical porosification of the p+ layers followed by a fast porous-Si strip. The intrinsic layers become channels; boron tails matter only until the sacrificial layers are gone.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 (no manufacturable 3D cell: epitaxial stack defects), A2 germanium chokepoint (China ~2/3 of refined Ge; Ga/Ge export-ban suspension ends 2026-11-27).
ideas.step_change_claim: Misfit 0.84% -> 0.05-0.16% (strain energy 30-260x lower), so tier count is no longer strain-limited; Ge per wafer 5-16x lower, or zero.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: Misfit: Si0.8Ge0.2 = 0.2 x 4.18% = 0.84%. B lattice contraction beta ~5.2e-24 cm3/atom [UNVERIFIED-PK] -> 0.052% at 1e20, 0.156% at 3e20; strain energy (prop. to eps^2) x0.0039-0.035. Ge to null it: 1.24-3.7% (16-5x less than 20%). B diffusion D = 0.76 exp(-3.46 eV/kT): 650 C epi for 10 h -> sqrt(Dt) = 0.6 nm (sharp); a 1,000 C, 10 s spike -> 3.9 nm, so sacrificial removal must come before any >900 C step. Selectivity needed for a 300-1,000 nm lateral recess with <=5 nm channel loss: >=100:1. (models/B3_3dprocess_estimates.py section B3-06)
